items.title: Add move-away behavior demo (CPU MuJoCo, stock walking policy)
items.body:
## Problem / use case

A common request for a small robot sharing floor space with people: when
someone walks towards it, get out of the way — but keep watching them, so the
robot can react if they change direction and so a human observer can tell the
robot has noticed them.

This PR adds that as a **CPU MuJoCo behavior demo**, not as production robot
autonomy. It shows how far a stock exported walking policy can be pushed with a
scripted supervisor, and it doubles as a rehearsal harness for the
velocity-command interface the runtime drives, in the spirit of
`scripts/infer_policy.py`.

**No new policy is trained, and no policy file is committed** — `--policy` is a
required argument.

## Implementation

Self-contained under `scripts/behavior_demos/move_away/`:

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `controller.py` | state machine + velocity-command law. Pure Python (no MuJoCo/ONNX/numpy) so it is fully unit-testable |
| `gaze.py` | camera-frame maths and the head visual servo |
| `perception.py` | field-of-view test + ray-cast occlusion check |
| `runtime.py` | scene path, default pose, observation layout, safe sensor lookup |
| `run_demo.py` | CLI entry point, simulation loop, optional rendering |
| `README.md` | measured constants, limitations, usage |

The behavior is `IDLE → RETREAT → TURN → CLEAR → DONE`. Heading is held
closed-loop in every walking state; the absolute trunk heading is measured each
tick and never integrated.

Also adds `src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/scene_move_away.xml`: `scene.xml`
plus a scripted **mocap** "person" prop. It is a mocap body with
`contype/conaffinity="0"`, so it adds **no degrees of freedom** (`nq` stays 21,
the keyframes stay valid) and it can never push the robot over. It follows the
existing `scene_ball.xml` pattern, so the `robot_allcollisions.xml` include
resolves the same way as the other scenes.

The observation is assembled as
`[base_ang_vel(3), projected_gravity(3), joint_pos(14), joint_vel(14), last_action(14), command(13)]`
= 61D. The demo writes only the `twist` slot and **zero-pads** `head_pose(4)` and
`body_pose(6)` rather than dropping them, per the shared-layout convention in
`AGENTS.md`.

`pyproject.toml` is unchanged. The headless path needs only `mujoco`,
`numpy` and `onnxruntime`, all already dependencies; `imageio`/`Pillow` are
imported lazily inside the rendering helper, so `--render-dir` is the only path
that needs them.

### One finding worth flagging

An earlier iteration of this demo looked up a gyro sensor named `imu_gyro`,
which **does not exist** in these models. `mujoco.mj_name2id` returns `-1` for an
unknown name, and `model.sensor_adr[-1]` is a *valid* index — the last sensor. So
the lookup did not raise: it silently fed `root_angmom` (subtree angular
momentum, kg·m²/s) into the slot the policy expects to hold rad/s.

The robot still walked and the rendered result looked plausible, which is what
makes this failure mode nasty. But every gait constant tuned against it described
the corrupted observation rather than the robot — including a "the `wz` sign is
inverted" conclusion that is simply not true with a real gyro.

Everything in this PR was re-measured against `imu_ang_vel`, and the constants
changed materially as a result:

| | against the bad observation | re-measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| retreat speed | `vx = -0.28` | `vx = -0.36` (gait does not engage above ≈ −0.30) |
| `wz` sign | reported inverted | **normal**, with real closed-loop authority |
| turn | open-loop, cut early at 45° | closed-loop, tracked to a 15° tolerance |

`runtime.sensor_address()` now raises on an unknown sensor name, and a
regression test pins it.

## Validation

Measured with a stock exported walking policy, defaults, 22 s:

| metric | value |
| --- | --- |
| final state | `DONE`, upright |
| person visible | **1100 / 1100** control steps (`lost_steps = 0`) |
| max off-axis angle | **2.3°** from camera centre |
| heading change | **+82.8°** (90° commanded) |
| trunk height | **z = 0.116** (nominal), min 0.114 |

Robustness spot-checks: `--turn-sign -1` mirrors the maneuver (−96.5°, still
1100/1100 visible); `--person-speed 0.20` keeps 1100/1100; `--seconds 28` stays
upright at 1400/1400. Rendered frames were inspected visually — the
picture-in-picture head-camera view keeps the person centred through the turn.

## Limitations — explicitly not claimed

- **The "person" is scripted, not perceived.** A mocap prop on a fixed straight
  path, its position read from simulator state. No detector, no tracker, no real
  sensing; the visibility test is purely geometric.
- **Gaze is kinematic only.** Head pose is applied in an isolated `MjData` copy
  used solely for perception and rendering, and is never fed back into the
  locomotion dynamics. The head is a large fraction of body mass and this policy
  was never trained to compensate an externally imposed head trajectory — driving
  it physically makes the robot fall. **This PR makes no claim of physical
  head-control stability while walking**, and the numbers above do not support
  one.
- **Sim only, CPU only.** Nothing here has been validated on hardware.
- Constants were measured against one exported walking policy in this scene;
  another policy would need its own sweep.
- The head-camera optical-frame correction (the MJCF exports a quaternion whose
  optical `-Z` points backwards into the robot's own CAD) is applied to the
  **in-memory** `MjModel` only. The committed MJCF is untouched — worth a
  maintainer opinion on whether the exported camera quaternion should be fixed
  upstream instead.

## Test plan

`tests/test_move_away_demo.py` — 25 tests, all CPU, **no policy file, no GPU and
no rendering context required**:

- **State machine**: IDLE holds until the person is both close *and* visible
  (range alone must not trigger); full `IDLE→RETREAT→TURN→CLEAR→DONE` ordering;
  IDLE/DONE command exactly zero velocity; retreat speed stays inside the
  measured engagement band; heading-hold sign opposes drift correctly; `wz`
  clamping; `turn_sign` direction; the `TURN_MAX` safety timeout; command
  low-pass filtering; angle wrapping.
- **Gaze maths**: MuJoCo optical-frame convention and handedness; bearing sign;
  elevation sign; frustum rejection behind and off-axis; servo error reduction;
  the head-pitch sign convention; joint-limit margins.
- **Observation contract**: exact 61D layout with the command block zero-padded.
- **Model invariants** (compile the MJCF only): the scene path resolves; 14
  actuators and `nq == 21` (the prop adds no DoF); the person is a
  non-colliding mocap body; the gyro sensor name resolves and is not the
  `sensor_adr[-1]` fallback, and a bad name raises; the optical correction
  aligns the camera with the trunk forward axis; robot and person body subtrees
  are disjoint; `DEFAULT_POSE` matches the scene's `STAND` keyframe.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_move_away_demo.py -q
25 passed

$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
179 passed, 1 skipped
```

`ruff check` is clean on the added files. (`ruff format` was deliberately not
run — the existing tree does not conform to its defaults, so applying it here
would produce unrelated churn.)

## Not included

No ONNX policy, no video and no GIF are committed — only text files.

## Demo video

Fresh render from commit `39506fff` after the `imu_ang_vel` sensor fix and controller re-measurement (22 s, 1,100 frames at 50 fps, 960×640). This is not the earlier render made with the invalid sensor lookup.

items.title: [Tasks] Add MicroDuck flat velocity walking task [4/6]
items.body:
# Description

Adds `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`: MicroDuck flat walking on Newton MJWarp with native BAM servos (#8161), ported from [microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl) through the original Lab MicroDuck task. It keeps that task's 14-joint action order, 61-value actor and 76-value critic inputs, 50 Hz control, rewards, command sampling, randomization, curricula, and PPO settings, so existing checkpoints load.

- Encoder bias is owned by the biased joint-position action term and IMU misalignment by its startup event term; observations read them from there.
- Joint velocity uses the core one-step `delay_min_lag`/`delay_max_lag`; `delayed_observation` only provides the IMU lag redrawn on a fixed 64-step period.
- Curricula use `modify_term_cfg` with one `staged_value` schedule; stages switch at `>=` their step (the old task used `>` for some, a one-step difference).
- Reuses core terms where they match (`body_projected_gravity_b`, `randomize_rigid_body_*`, `randomize_joint_parameters`, `push_by_setting_velocity`, `joint_pos_limits`, `action_rate_l2`, `bad_orientation`, `UniformVelocityCommand`). Task-local rewards keep upstream's formulas, which differ from the nearest core terms: tracking combines planar and off-axis error in one kernel, `body_ang_vel_xy_l2` uses the world-frame trunk rate, `foot_slip` squares contact speed, and `self_collision_cost` reads the filtered force matrix.
- MJWarp line search uses 50 iterations instead of 20; 20 repeatedly exhausted the current solver.
- Critic foot observations, the upright reward and a termination guard against non-finite MJWarp states, which occurred under heavy contact in the original task.
- The environment-browser preview image is served from the docs image host (to be uploaded), not committed.

**Stacked on #8266.** [Task-only diff](https://github.com/AntoineRichard/IsaacLab/compare/antoiner/feat/bam-backlash...antoiner/feat/microduck-flat-velocity).

## Type of change

- New feature

## Validation

Runs used a local mirror of the `isaac-dev` Nucleus MicroDuck assets until the public S3 mirror syncs.

- `uv run python -m pytest source/isaaclab_tasks/test/test_microduck_velocity.py` — 1 passed (61/76 inputs, policy term order, action joint order, per-reset BAM friction draw). These guard the deployed ONNX interface: a reorder against the USD's different joint order silently breaks shipped checkpoints, which stepping tests cannot see. Stepping is covered by `test_contrib_environments_kitless.py`; 100 random-action steps stayed finite here.
- Joint-velocity delay check without noise: the observation equals the previous step's joint velocity exactly.
- Curriculum check: at the last stage, action-rate weight −1.0, head-bias weight −3.0, standing fraction 0.25, widest head ranges, and CoM ranges ±0.015/±0.01 m; encoder bias and IMU misalignment sampled into their owners.
- Supplied `velocity_flat.onnx` (original Lab checkpoint, iteration 49,999), 32 envs × 1,000 control steps:

| Playback condition | Falls | Timeouts | Mean planar velocity error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed 0.15 m/s forward, play mode | 0 | 32 | 0.136 m/s |
| Training commands, corruption and disturbances | 0 | 32 | 0.185 m/s |

  This shows the existing policy runs stably, not exact parity with the old dynamics.
- `uv run isaaclab -f`

## Not in this PR

- Rough and backlash variants (#8270), recovery task (#8271).

## Follow-ups

- Replace `delayed_observation` with core `ObservationTermCfg.delay_*`. Kept for parity: the IMU lag is redrawn on a fixed 64-step period with a per-environment phase, whereas core redraws with a per-sample hold probability.
- Find the source of the occasional non-finite MJWarp states and drop the observation guards; reset-time CoM randomization on Newton is a candidate.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guidelines and ran `uv run isaaclab -f`
- [x] Validated with focused coverage and the test-audit criteria
- [x] Added a changelog fragment for `isaaclab_tasks`

items.title: strands-robots v1: The design and part-by-part refactor
items.body:
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Pinned. This is the v1 contract; the dates are in the roadmap, #3818.** Every v1 pull request says `Part N of #4749` and does exactly one part from [the plan](#the-plan-part-by-part). A PR that has to leave this design writes the change here as a comment *before* making it. Decisions 15-19 were added on Oct 15; the old body is preserved in the comments. ## v1 in one sentence **A `Simulation` is a world. A `Robot` is a body in a world, or on a bus. A `Policy` turns an `Observation` into an `Action`.** Everything else (the mesh, tools, recording, the dashboard) is written once against those three and never again per backend. ```python from strands import Agent from strands_robots import Mesh, Policy, Robot, Simulation arm = Robot("so101") # joins Simulation.default() g1 = Robot("g1", position=[1, 0, 0]) # the SAME world assert arm.sim is g1.sim arm.act({"shoulder_pan": 0.3}) # one control step of world time g1.run(Policy("holosoma"), seconds=10) # observe -> policy -> act, written once arm.run(Policy("zenoh://gpu:7447/smolvla"), instruction="pick the cube", seconds=20) # any lerobot-policy-server sim = Simulation("isaac", device="cuda:0") # pick another world explicitly arm2 = Robot("so101", sim=sim) batch = Simulation(physics="newton", num_envs=1024) real = Robot("so101", port="/dev/tty.usbmodem...", confirm=operator_says_yes) real.calibrate() # LeRobot calibration JSON, unchanged real.estop() # from any thread; always wins; resume(approved_by=) releases it lab = Mesh("zenoh://", tenant="lab-a") # every robot on the LAN, zero config lab.mount(real) Agent(tools=[arm.tool, g1.tool, sim.tool, lab.tool])("look around, then wave") ``` --- ## Why Read against `main` @ `5386b9c0` (v0.5.3 + 1): - **`Robot` is not a class.** `robot.py:636` is a factory typed `-> Simulation | HardwareRobot | HardwareDriver`. In sim mode it builds a world and returns the engine, so the "robot" you hold is a `MuJoCoSimEngine` (8,125 lines, 110 methods, 9 bases) with one robot in it. - **Two robots means two worlds.** `Robot("so101")` then `Robot("g1")` gives two engines that cannot see each other; the dashboard runs a process per card stitched back over the mesh (979-line `DeviceManager`). - **Isaac makes the current model impossible.** `SimulationApp` can exist once per process; a second Isaac robot silently gets the first app. - **Newton is a solver, not a world**, yet it is a third 3,179-line `SimEngine` that copies scene loading, cameras, recording and randomization. - **Sim and hardware share no type**, so the policy runner, recorder, teleop and mesh were each written twice, and safety lives in three side modules instead of on the robot. Result: 260,105 lines in the package. The v1 reference does the whole job, safety and mesh included, in **10,459**. --- ## The design ### 1. One world `Simulation.default()` is process-global, like `asyncio.get_event_loop()`. It is created on first use: MuJoCo, headless. ### 2. Five types `Description` (what a robot is), `Simulation` (a world), `Robot` (a body in it, or on a bus), `Policy` (what it does next) and `Body`, the only thing that differs between a simulated, a real and a remote robot. ### 3. One loop `Robot.run` is written once. It checks the policy's `Requirements` and units before step one, and ends with a `RunResult` that says why it stopped: `steps`, `stop_when`, `stopped`, `fault` (the policy gave up) or `estop`. ### 4. Thirteen methods make a simulator ### 5. A real robot brings its twin ### 6. A robot is a device Every robot, sim or real, generates its own **manifest** (sensors, controls with `range`, `safe` and `on_disconnect`, rpcs, events). Every write that is not the developer's own code passes **one safety chain**: range, safe, interlocks, validators, the operator gate. `estop()` bypasses the chain, takes no lock, and latches until `resume(approved_by=)`. ### 7. Any robot, anywhere: the mesh ### 8. Any policy, any robot ### 9. The dashboard is a twin of one world ### 10. One concept, one package --- ## The interfaces The whole top level is `strands_robots.__all__`: ```python Robot, Simulation, Policy, Body, Description, Observation, Action, JointState, Pose, Mesh, __version__ ``` Everything else is imported from the package that owns it: `strands_robots.simulation`, `.robot.device`, `.robot.safety`, `.robot.drivers`, `.policy`, `.policy.lerobot`, `.mesh`, `.recording`, `.tools`, `.dashboard`, `.units`.
Simulation: one world, owns time, holds many robots ```python class Simulation: def __init__(self, backend: str = "mujoco", *, physics: str = "native", # "native" | "newton" (MuJoCo-Warp) timestep: float = 0.002, substeps: int = 10, headless: bool = True, device: str | None = None, num_envs: int = 1, # > 1 needs physics="newton" gravity=(0, 0, -9.81), ground: bool = True, render_size=(640, 480)) -> None @classmethod def default(cls) -> Simulation # the world a Robot joins when given none # time def step(self, n: int = 1) -> None def control_step(self) -> None # what one act() costs a simulated robot def manual_time(self) -> ContextManager[Simulation] def reset(self, *, keyframe: str | None = None, seed: int | None = None) -> None time: float; physics: Physics; envs: int; revision: int; lock: RLock # scene robots: Mapping[str, Robot] def add(self, robot, *, position=None, orientation=None, keyframe=None) -> Robot # Robot.__init__ calls it def remove(self, robot: Robot | str) -> None def add_object(self, name, *, shape=None, path=None, size=None, position=None, mass=None, color=None) -> Object def set_pose(self, body: Robot | Object | str, position=None, orientation=None) -> None # teleport def camera(self, name, *, position, target=None, fov=45, size=None, attach=None) -> SceneCamera def render(self, camera=None) -> np.ndarray def randomize(self, *, friction=None, mass=None, lighting=None, seed=None) -> None def contacts(self) -> list[Contact] # loop, agents, lifecycle def run(self, policies: Mapping[Robot, Policy], **run_options) -> dict[str, RunResult] # lock-step def describe(self) -> dict # robots, objects, cameras, physics, time: the dashboard reads THIS tool: AgentTool # add robot/object/camera, step, reset, render (an image back) def close(self) -> None # also a context manager ``` `Simulation("isaac")` steps PhysX under its one `SimulationApp` (a second one in the process is refused until `close()`); `physics="newton"` belongs to the MuJoCo backend. Both are imported only when such a world is made.
Backend: the only thing a new simulator implements ```python class Backend(ABC): def load(self, scene: Scene) -> None # (re)build from plain data; joint state of surviving bodies carried over def step(self, n: int) -> None def reset(self, keyframe: str | None) -> None def time(self) -> float def joint_state(self, body: str) -> JointState def set_targets(self, body: str, targets: np.ndarray) -> None def body_pose(self, body: str) -> Pose # floating bodies fill linear/angular velocity def set_pose(self, body: str, pose: Pose, *, zero_velocity: bool = True) -> None def set_gains(self, body: str, kp: np.ndarray, kd: np.ndarray) -> None # a policy's PD travels with the policy def render(self, camera: str) -> np.ndarray def contacts(self) -> list[Contact] def physics(self) -> Physics def close(self) -> None ``` Implementations live under `strands_robots/simulation/backends/{mujoco,isaac,newton}/`. mjlab is not a backend: it is `Simulation(physics="newton", num_envs=N)`.
Robot: the one type a user holds ```python class Robot: def __init__(self, name: str, *, # registry key ("so101", "g1", ...) or a path to MJCF/URDF sim: Simulation | None = None, # None -> Simulation.default(), unless port=/driver= is given port: str | None = None, driver: str | Driver | None = None, cameras: Mapping[str, int | str] | None = None, # hardware only position=None, orientation=None, keyframe: str | None = None, id: str | None = None, # unique in its world: so101, so101_2, ... twin: bool = True, # hardware: a free twin in Simulation.default() confirm: Callable[[np.ndarray], bool] | None = None, # hardware: the operator gate mesh: Mesh | None = None) # sugar for mesh.mount(robot) # the verbs def observe(self, *, images: bool = True) -> Observation def act(self, action: Action, *, steps: int | None = None) -> Observation # the developer's own call def confirm_act(self, action: Action, *, steps=None, confirmed=False) -> Observation # what tools, the mesh and # the dashboard call: through the safety chain def calibrate(self, *, interactive: bool = True) -> Calibration # the loop, written once for every body def run(self, policy, *, instruction=None, hz=None, seconds=None, steps=None, stop_when=None, units="auto", realtime=False, record=None, push=False) -> RunResult # hz: the policy's, else 30 def start(self, policy, **run_options) -> Task # background: Task.stop() / .status / .result def stop(self) -> RunResult | None # a robot is a device manifest: Manifest # generated from the Description and the body def describe(self) -> dict # the manifest as JSON + live task and estop state def estop(self) -> None # any thread, no chain, no lock; latches def resume(self, *, approved_by: str) -> None # only a named operator releases the latch def hold(self) -> None def subscribe(self, event: str, cb, *, hz=None) -> Callable[[], None] # "state": the observation's joints, t, seq estopped: bool; supports_position_hold: bool # placement (sim only; hardware raises, its twin can still be teleported) pose: Pose def set_pose(self, position=None, orientation=None) -> None def set_gains(self, kp, kd) -> None # identity and agents name: str; id: str; description: Description; sim: Simulation | None; body: Body is_real: bool; twin: Robot | None; twin_of: Robot | None; action_keys: tuple[str, ...] tool: AgentTool # generated from the manifest's rpcs def close(self) -> None ```
Data: Observation, Action, JointState, Pose, and the types that live with their owner ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class Observation: t: float joints: JointState # names + positions / velocities / efforts (SI: rad, rad/s, N·m) pose: Pose | None # base pose in the world frame (+ twist for floating bases) images: Mapping[str, np.ndarray] # camera -> HxWx3 uint8 extras: Mapping[str, Any] # imu, contacts, battery ... per body def __getitem__(self, joint: str) -> float def to_lerobot(self) -> dict # "observation.state", "observation.images." Action = np.ndarray | Mapping[str, float] # joint targets in Description.action_keys order; validated once, in Robot.act @dataclass(frozen=True) class Pose: position; orientation # (w, x, y, z); linear_velocity, angular_velocity: optional # with their owner (decision 14) strands_robots.policy.Requirements # images {cam: (w, h)}, state_dim; checked before step one, refused by name strands_robots.robot.run.RunResult # steps, seconds, hz_target, hz_achieved, stopped_by, recorded, final, fault strands_robots.robot.drivers.Calibration # LeRobot's calibration JSON, read and written as is strands_robots.simulation.Physics, Contact, Scene, Object ```
Policy: one factory, picked by the form of the spec ```python class Policy: # Policy(spec) returns the right subclass; subclassing it is a plain constructor def act(self, obs: Observation, *, instruction: str | None = None) -> Action def reset(self) -> None def requirements(self) -> Requirements units: str | None # a unit scheme ("rad", "lerobot"), or units_for(description) for a checkpoint # optional hooks the run loop honours: attach(robot) / detach(), hz, realtime, gains = (kp, kd) Policy(lambda obs: ...) # any callable Policy("holosoma") # ONNX presets (strands_robots/policy/onnx/presets.json, data): Policy("microduck", vx=0.3) # holosoma (G1) and the ten microduck skills: Policy("microduck?skill=roulade") # alpha_walking velstand alpha_stand alpha_sitstand ball_kick_left/right from_spec("microduck?skill=velstand&wz=1") # roller roller_crouch roulade alpha_ground_pick Policy("lerobot/smolvla_base") # a LeRobot checkpoint in-process, through LeRobot's own load_deployment Policy("zenoh://gpu:7447/smolvla") # any lerobot-policy-server, through LeRobot's own client (chunks, RTC) ChunkedPolicy(inner, replan_every=None) # holds an action chunk and replays it; lives in policy/, never in the sim from strands_robots.policy.lerobot import server_config, write_server_yaml, serve server_config(robot.description, "lerobot/smolvla_base") # the server's YAML from the robot + the checkpoint ``` A LeRobot deployment's names (`.pos`), cameras and units (its `semantics` label, mapped by `units/semantics.json`) are checked against the robot **before a session exists**; a lost server, a deadline or a stale chunk raises `PolicyFault` and the run ends `stopped_by="fault"`.
Device and safety: strands_robots.robot.device, strands_robots.robot.safety ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class Manifest: device_id: str; device_type: str; name: str; real: bool; position_hold: bool tenant: str; labels: Mapping[str, str]; twin: str | None; twin_of: str | None sensors: tuple[Sensor, ...] #
Driver: a hardware Body ```python class Driver(Protocol): names: tuple[str, ...] # the Description's action_keys, in order def read(self) -> JointState def write(self, targets: np.ndarray) -> None def pose(self) -> Pose | None def images(self) -> Mapping[str, np.ndarray] def extras(self) -> Mapping[str, Any] def hold(self) -> None # keep the current positions under torque def estop(self) -> None # the fastest stop the bus has; takes no world or run-loop lock def calibrate(self, *, interactive: bool = True) -> Calibration # LeRobot's calibration JSON, read and written as is def close(self) -> None supports_position_hold: bool # registry hardware.position_hold, else the driver's own answer ``` 1.0 drivers: `feetech` (SO-100/101: read, write, torque, calibrate; exact LeRobot `degrees` from a calibration), `unitree` (G1/Go2/H1 over DDS: observe), `microduck` (robotd: observe). The driver is registry data (`hardware.driver`).
Mesh: every device, anywhere (from strands_robots import Mesh) ```python class Mesh: def __init__(self, transports="zenoh://", *, tenant=None, presence_ttl=3.0, operator=None, resume_authority=None, resume_key=None) # "zenoh://", "iot://us-west-2", "memory://", or several def mount(self, robot, *, device_id=None, labels=None, state_hz=None, watchdog_ms=500.0) def unmount(self, device_id: str) -> None def discover(self, selector="device(*)", *, min_count=0, timeout=0.0) -> list[Device] # device(role:arm,type:robot_arm) def invoke(self, device_id: str, rpc: str, *, timeout=2.0, **args) # through ITS safety chain def subscribe(self, device_id: str, event: str, cb) -> Callable[[], None] # "state": same payload as in-process def connect(self, device_id: str, *, images=False) -> Robot # a Robot whose Body is a RemoteBody def broadcast(self, command, *, selector="device(*)", deadline=1.0, approved_by=None) -> list[str] # who acked tool: AgentTool # use_mesh, generated from the manifests present def close(self) -> None ``` Keys (zenoh): `strands///{manifest,state,event/,rpc/}` and liveliness `strands//@presence/`; scouting only on `224.0.0.224:7447`. Over AWS IoT Core rpcs are confirmed Direct Messages, so a device that is away answers 404 at once and nothing is queued. A device whose controller vanishes applies `on_disconnect`; resume is the stopping operator's (in-process / loopback) or a fresh Ed25519-signed assertion.
Recording, tools, dashboard ```python robot.run(policy, seconds=10, record="datasets/so101") # LeRobot v3 through LeRobot's own writer; robot.run(policy, seconds=10, record="hf://me/so101", push=True) # one episode per run, resumable; meta/units.json says # which units; only hf:// with push=True uploads robot.tool, sim.tool, mesh.tool # strands agent tools, generated from the manifest and # the verbs; an agent can estop, never resume or calibrate from strands_robots.dashboard import Dashboard Dashboard(sim, robots=[real], model=..., mesh=lab).serve(port=8090) # GET /api/scene, WS /ws/state, WS /ws/chat, # POST /api/robots/{id}/act (X-Confirm on a real body); # loopback only; standalone in the browser with no server ```
--- ## Decisions | # | question | decision | |---|---|---| | 1 | default world | `Simulation.default()`, process-global. A hardware `Robot(port=)` also gets a free twin there (`robot.twin`); `twin=False` turns it off. | | 2 | time | `act()` advances its world one control step; `sim.manual_time()` hands stepping to the caller; `sim.run({...})` for lock-step. | | 3 | mjlab | not a backend: `Simulation(physics="newton", num_envs=N)`. | | 4 | name | `Simulation` (attribute `robot.sim`). | | 5 | teleport | `set_pose` is in the Backend contract; sim only. | | 6 | gains | `Backend.set_gains`: a policy's PD is part of the policy. The G1 stands under holosoma's kp/kd and falls under the MJCF's kp=500. | | 7 | operator gate | `Robot(confirm=)`. A tool's `confirm=true` is the model's intent: it never replaces the operator's callable. A real robot with no callable cannot be moved by any tool. Since decision 16 the gate is the last step of the safety chain. | | 8 | e-stop over IoT | a Direct Message: reaches a connected robot or fails with 404 at once. Never a retained command that fires on a robot booting later. | | 9 | heavy imports | core imports nothing from `isaacsim`, `newton`, `warp`, `lerobot`, `torch`, `zenoh`, `onnxruntime`, `strands`, `fastapi` at module load; adapters import lazily and name the extra to install. | | 10 | recording | `run(record=dir \| "hf://owner/name")` writes LeRobot v3 through LeRobot's own writer. Only `hf://` with `push=True` touches the Hub. | | 11 | no sibling packages | training, ROS, Foxglove, teleop, benchmarks and eval come back **inside** `strands_robots`, on the v1 interfaces, after 1.0. | | 12 | drivers in 1.0 | feetech (SO-100/101), unitree (G1, Go2, H1), microduck. Every other driver is ported after 1.0. | | 13 | where v1 is built | on the `dev` branch, from an empty package; modules at their final paths; no compatibility shim. `main` keeps v0.5.x until `dev` becomes `main`. | | 14 | one concept, one package | each concept is a package with its implementations inside (`simulation/backends/`, `robot/drivers/`, `robot/run/`, `policy/`, `mesh/`, ...); `types/` keeps `JointState`, `Action`, `Pose`, `Observation`; robot facts are registry data; ≤ 250 lines per file; import-linter guards the edges (#4772). | | 15 | remote inference | **LeRobot's own protocol over Zenoh**: `Policy("zenoh://host:port/")` through LeRobot's `RemoteClient`, and checkpoints in-process through LeRobot's `load_deployment`. No re-implementation of LeRobot. `Policy("ws://...")` is after 1.0. Until LeRobot ships remote inference on PyPI, `[lerobot]` pins only Zenoh (`>=1.9,<1.10`) and LeRobot `main` is installed by hand. | | 16 | a robot is a device | every Robot generates a manifest; every non-developer write passes one safety chain; `estop()` bypasses it, takes no lock and latches until `resume(approved_by=)`; the watchdog applies `on_disconnect`. Tools, the mesh and the dashboard are generated from the manifest (part 5.5). | | 17 | the mesh | `Mesh` replaces `Fleet` and `Transport`: mount, discover, invoke, subscribe, connect, broadcast, over zenoh or AWS IoT Core; `use_mesh` for agents; `mesh.connect(id)` replaces `Robot.connect(url)`. | | 18 | no migration guide | strands-robots is a Labs project: v1 has no backwards-compatibility promise, no shim and no migration page. The docs site lands on `dev` with the parts (part 12 does not wait for part 11). | | 19 | the public surface | `__all__` is the eleven names above (the nine types, `Mesh` and `__version__`); every other type is imported from its package. | ## What moves where | today (`strands_robots/…`) | lines | v1 | |---|---:|---| | `robot.py` factory, `hardware_robot.py` | 1,303 + 4,674 | `robot/`: `Robot`, `SimBody`, the run loop in `robot/run/`, `robot/device/`, `robot/safety/` | | `simulation/` (`mujoco`, `newton`, `isaac`, `mjlab`, base `SimEngine`) | 76,830 | `simulation/` (written once) + `simulation/backends/{mujoco,isaac,newton}/` | | `policies/` (18 providers) | 31,280 | `policy/`: `lerobot/` (in-process + Zenoh), `onnx/` (presets as data), `chunked.py`, `factory.py` | | `drivers/` (30 robots) | 34,613 | `robot/drivers/`: **feetech, unitree, microduck in 1.0**, the rest after | | `mesh/`, `device_connect/`, `rtps/`, `rosbridge.py` | 22,641 + 2,866 + … | `mesh/` (+ `mesh/transports/{zenoh,iot,memory}`); ROS returns as a transport after 1.0 | | `tools/` (hand-written specs ×3) | 17,366 | `tools/`: generated from the manifest; `use_mesh` in `mesh/tool.py` | | `_command_gate.py`, `_motion_grants.py`, `_hitl_audit.py` | 1,500+ | `robot/safety/` + `confirm=` | | `dataset_*.py`, `recorder.py`, `verify_dataset.py` | 4,000+ | `recording/` (LeRobot v3) | | `dashboard/` (process per card) | 23,657 | `dashboard/`: one world, four routes, MuJoCo WASM twin, standalone mode | | `registry/` | 2,758 | the same JSON + device and hardware facts, read by `Description` | | `training/`, `foxglove/`, `teleop*`, `ros*`, benchmarks, eval | 13,542 + … | after 1.0, inside `strands_robots` (v0.5.x keeps them meanwhile) | --- ## The plan, part by part Each part is one PR against **`dev`**. Merged parts are on `dev`; the open parts are a stack of drafts, each on the one below it, merged lowest first once its review approves after the last push and the required check is green. | part | scope | gate (a test in the PR) | state | |---|---|---|---| | **0** | empty `dev`: skeleton, CI, changelog convention, drawing toolkit | lint + one test; drawings verify | merged #4754 | | **1** | `types/` + `description/` over the registry JSON | every registry robot loads a `Description`; nothing heavy at import | merged #4755 | | **2** | `Simulation`, `Backend`, `simulation/backends/mujoco/` | the shared-world test | merged #4756 | | **3** | `Robot` is a class: `SimBody`, `run/start/stop`, `set_pose`, twin and gate plumbing | `type(Robot("so101")) is Robot`; `run()` returns a `RunResult` | merged #4757 | | **3.5** | one concept, one package; units as registry data (decision 14) | tests unchanged but imports; ≤ 250 lines; import-linter | merged #4772 | | **4** | `Policy`: factory, `ChunkedPolicy`, `from_spec`; LeRobot in-process + over Zenoh; ONNX (holosoma, ten microduck skills) | SmolVLA drives so101 through `run()`; local vs served ACT parity; holosoma G1 pelvis ≥ 0.74 m for 10 s; `microduck?vx=0.3` walks ≥ 1 m | **#4773** | | **5** | `Driver`: feetech, unitree, microduck; free twin; `Robot(confirm=)` | bus read-only test on a real SO-101; operator says no → nothing written | merged #4758 (+ check 9, #4771) | | **5.5** | a Robot is a device: manifest, safety chain, estop, watchdog (decision 16) | every registry robot builds a manifest; refusals name joint + value + bound; estop stops a run within one tick | **#4774** | | **6** | `simulation/backends/{isaac,newton}/` | on a GPU box: two robots in one Isaac world; `num_envs=1024` | **#4775** | | **7** | the mesh: `Mesh`, zenoh, AWS IoT Core, `use_mesh` (decision 17) | 3 processes discover each other; invoke through the chain; one e-stop for all; real IoT round trip, offline = 404 | **#4776** | | **8** | agent tools generated from the manifest | a real strands Agent turn calls observe then act; a real robot's act through a tool passes the gate | **#4778** | | **9** | `run(record=)` → LeRobot v3 | 3 episodes with a camera reload in a fresh process; a second run resumes | **#4777** | | **10** | dashboard: one world, four routes, MuJoCo WASM twin, standalone mode | Playwright: both robots painted; server `act()` in the twin < 200 ms; runtime add; chat `tool_use`; standalone duck walks in the browser | **#4779** | | **acc** | the acceptance suite, the 1.0 definition (15 checks; check 9 on the arm) | green on `dev` in one command | **#4780** | | **12** | docs site + notebooks (decision 18) | `mkdocs build --strict`; every page's first example runs | **#4781** | | **11** | `dev` becomes `main`: one release PR; `v0.5.x` branch cut first | the acceptance suite green on `dev`; size report (`main` before → after) | after the stack | Every other driver and policy provider is ported **after 1.0** against the interfaces above, one issue each, closed with a measurement on the hardware or the checkpoint. ### Rules for every part 1. **One part, one PR.** Title `v1 part N: `, body starts with `Part N of #4749`, a `changelog.d/` fragment. 2. **Failing test first.** The gate test lands red in the first commit, green in the last. 3. **Measured, not claimed.** The PR body quotes the command and its output for every number in it. 4. **No `**kwargs` swallowing.** Every keyword is named in the signature or refused. 5. **Core imports nothing heavy** at module load (decision 9). 6. **Sim never imports policies; policies never import a backend.** `Robot.run` is where they meet. 7. **No hardware motion** without the operator gate and a human at the robot. 8. **Deviations are written here first**, as a comment, then made. --- ## Evidence: the reference implementation Built and measured before the PRs went up (`cagataycali/robots-harness/robots-v1-2`, the code the stack lands): | what | measured | |---|---| | size | 10,459 lines vs 260,105 (4%);
