items.title: [Newton] Add BAM servo actuator and MicroDuck walking tasks
items.body:
# Description

Adds a Newton-native [BAM](https://github.com/Rhoban/bam) servo actuator, Pollen Robotics' MicroDuck built on it (with gearbox-backlash variants), and MicroDuck flat and rough velocity walking tasks. This combines the former stack #8161, #8265, #8266 and #8267, which are closed in favor of this PR.

### BAM servo actuator (`isaaclab`, `isaaclab_newton`)

BAM is an identified voltage-domain model of small smart servos (firmware P loop, PWM, DC motor, supply sag, command delay, load-dependent gearbox friction) for sim-to-real on low-cost legged robots.

- `BamActuatorCfg` / `BamMotorCfg` (core) configure the fit and deployment settings; authoring writes `NewtonBamDriveAPI` actuator prims.
- `isaaclab_newton.actuators.DriveBam` is a Newton `DriveBase` running Warp kernels each physics step; CUDA-graph safe, per-environment delay streams and supply.
- `MjWarpActuatorBridge` publishes the friction budget into MJWarp `dof_frictionloss` and reads the previous solve's external load. BAM requires Newton + MJWarp + `use_newton_actuators=True`; other backends and solvers, including CPU MuJoCo, raise.
- `NewtonManager.register_pre_actuator_callback` / `register_solver_init_callback` hooks for solver-coupled drives. Hard resets discard pre-actuator hooks with the other per-model hooks, and BAM binds again on the new model.
- **Backlash:** `BamActuatorCfg.backlash_joint_template` names each servo's passive play hinge (e.g. `"passive_{}_backlash"`). The firmware then measures servo angle plus play angle; motor velocity, friction, and applied torque stay on the servo joint. Authoring writes `newton:hasBacklash` on every BAM prim (1 when the template is set, 0 otherwise) so backlash and regular drives never merge, and the MJWarp binding resolves each hinge per world before graph capture; missing or non-revolute pairs raise.
- Each Newton BAM drive takes the start-up settings of the groups it drives, so groups in separate drives (e.g. different `max_delay`) can use their own supply ranges and backlash; groups that share a drive must agree. A supply sagged to 0 V applies no voltage, leaving only back-EMF braking.
- **Deprecated:** Newton-native actuators follow the Newton 1.6 drive API, so `read_group_parameter` / `write_group_parameter` address the component as `"drive"`. `"controller"` still resolves to the drive and emits a `DeprecationWarning`; it is scheduled for removal in 3.2.

- Native actuator authoring reactivates a replaced `NewtonActuator` prim whose path matches one it deactivated; before, the joint silently kept no actuator. This applies to every Newton-native actuator config, not only BAM.

Core keeps only the config and USD authoring; all Newton/MJWarp code lives in `isaaclab_newton`. The backend check in authoring uses `FactoryBase._get_backend()`, as `base_visualizer.py` does, since `SimulationContext.backend` reports the tensor backend.

### MicroDuck asset (`isaaclab_assets`)

- `MICRODUCK_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ALLCOLLISIONS_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ROLLERS_CFG` with Dynamixel XL330 BAM servos: the `m6` fit from Rhoban BAM `62bd8ce`, firmware gain, nominal and sampled supply voltage, supply sag, and a 3–6-step command delay, shared by all variants.
- `MICRODUCK_BACKLASH_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ALLCOLLISIONS_BACKLASH_CFG`, `MICRODUCK_ROLLERS_BACKLASH_CFG` use `replace(..., backlash_joint_template=...)` with the `*_backlash.usd` assets (14 ±1° play hinges; 28/28/32 joints). Inserting the play links removed the all-collisions variant's implicit shin–sole exclusions; the USD now authors those two pairs explicitly.
- Variants are `clone` + USD path overrides, like the Unitree H1 variants. The roller variant leaves its four wheel joints passive and starts 2 cm higher to clear them.
- USDs load from `ISAACLAB_NUCLEUS_DIR/Robots/PollenRobotics/MicroDuck/` (with `ATTRIBUTION.txt` and `LICENSE`).
- `MICRODUCK_JOINT_NAMES` lists the 14 servos in the robot's servo order (left leg, neck and head, right leg), with leg and head subsets; every USD lists the right leg first, so tasks select them with `preserve_order=True`.
- `test_valid_configs.py`: articulations with BAM actuators spawn on Newton MJWarp through a one-environment clone plan, since BAM runs on no other backend. Other assets are unchanged.

### Walking tasks (`isaaclab_tasks`)

`IsaacContrib-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` and `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck`, ported from [microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl) through the original Lab MicroDuck task. Both keep its 14-joint action order, 61-value actor and 76-value critic inputs, 50 Hz control, rewards, command sampling, randomization, curricula, and PPO settings, so existing checkpoints load.

- Encoder bias is owned by the biased joint-position action term and IMU misalignment by its startup event term; observations read them from there.
- Joint velocity uses the core one-step `delay_min_lag`/`delay_max_lag`; `delayed_observation` only provides the IMU lag redrawn on a fixed 64-step period.
- Curricula use `modify_term_cfg` with one `staged_value` schedule; stages switch at `>=` their step (the old task used `>` for some, a one-step difference).
- Reuses core terms where they match (`body_projected_gravity_b`, `randomize_rigid_body_*`, `randomize_joint_parameters`, `push_by_setting_velocity`, `joint_pos_limits`, `action_rate_l2`, `bad_orientation`, `UniformVelocityCommand`). Task-local rewards keep upstream's formulas, which differ from the nearest core terms: tracking combines planar and off-axis error in one kernel, `body_ang_vel_xy_l2` uses the world-frame trunk rate, `foot_slip` squares contact speed, and `self_collision_cost` reads the filtered force matrix.
- MJWarp uses 100 solver iterations and 50 line-search iterations instead of microduck_rl's 10 and 20; the original budgets were exhausted with the current solver.
- Critic foot observations, rewards and a termination guard against non-finite MJWarp states, which microduck_rl's rough velocity task hit under heavy contact. Rewards run before resets, so the reward terms stay finite on the step a diverged environment is terminated.
- **Rough terrain:** [microduck_rl's gentle mix](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl/blob/8d0db74916a4f833d1d9b95d6a1d7f4d13b9d5ec/src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py) (25% flat, 25% stairs ≤1.5 cm, 30% random grid ≤1 cm, 20% slopes 0.03–0.10) with the existing distance-based terrain curriculum. It is a new mix rather than `ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` because the steps are centimeter-scale. The actor stays blind; two downward rays per foot give the critic and foot rewards the ground height, handling missed rays and step undersides.
- Lab builds triangle-mesh terrain instead of mjlab's boxes, so a task-local `TerrainImporter` subclass authors upstream's softer MuJoCo contact (`solref=(0.04, 1.0)`) on the terrain mesh; `TerrainImporterCfg` has no collision-property field yet. The rough task uses 200 contacts and 1024 constraint rows per environment.
- **Backlash preset:** `presets=backlash` switches either task to the backlash robot and, together, the output-side encoder observations, head-pose rewards, a servo-only joint-limit penalty, and a separate experiment name. One `_backlash_preset` helper builds each pair, so no backlash task IDs, environment subclasses, or runner subclasses are added.
- The environment-browser preview is committed under `environment-previews/`, following develop's convention for ground-plane tasks; the rough row reuses the flat still until a rough-terrain capture exists. Both rows list the `backlash` preset.

### Newton model updates (`isaaclab_newton`)

- Batches pending model-change flags into one solver notification before stepping. MicroDuck queues armature (`JOINT_DOF_PROPERTIES`) and CoM (`BODY_INERTIAL_PROPERTIES`) changes on every reset, and `SolverMuJoCo` reruns `set_const_0` and the solref update for each flag, so one combined notification halves that work.

  | Flat MicroDuck, 4096 envs, idle RTX 5090 | Per-flag notify (develop) | Batched |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Env step, median | 20.8 ms | 15.9 ms |
  | Model-change notification per env step | 10.2 ms | 5.4 ms |

  Median of 8 alternating rounds of 100 env steps after 100 warmup steps, in one process; every round showed a 4.6–5.0 ms gap. About 100 environments reset per env step, so notification runs on nearly every step. The resulting model matches the per-flag path to float32 roundoff.

## Type of change

- New feature
- Deprecation (`"controller"` → `"drive"` group-parameter component)

## Validation

Run on an RTX 5090 with the branch merged into `develop` at `2224495d` (Isaac Sim 6.2, Newton `5ea82eef`, MuJoCo Warp 3.14), in a `uv sync --locked --extra isaacsim --extra test --extra skrl --extra all --extra teleop` environment. BAM fixtures (`ISAACLAB_NUCLEUS_DIR/Tests/BAM/`: two USDs, upstream BAM `62bd8ce` goldens, recorded pendulum trajectory) and the MicroDuck USDs loaded from the default public asset root.

- `test_bam_actuator.py` — 32 passed (goldens: motor, friction, supply sag, mjlab delay replay; authoring; reset/RNG/graph replay; play-angle feedback with non-zero rotor velocity; unbound play hinge; supply exhausted to 0 V).
- `test_bam_actuator_mjwarp.py` — 14 passed (live MJWarp pendulum vs recorded trajectory, decimation 1/2; multi-articulation merge, re-bound after hard resets without accumulating hooks; per-group settings on separate and shared drives; solver and CPU MuJoCo rejection; missing play hinge). Without the hard-reset fix the hook check fails (pre-actuator hooks 1 → 2).
- `test_newton_adapter.py` — 17 passed; `test_actuator_collection.py` — 30 passed (including the `"controller"` deprecation warning at the caller's line); `test_newton_actuators_newton.py` (Isaac Sim) — 37 passed.
- `test_microduck.py` — 7 passed: all six variants spawn and step (14 servos, passive joints undriven), and the backlash test sets a distinct play angle per joint and environment and checks the analytic servo effort.
- `test_valid_configs.py` (Isaac Sim) — passed; BAM entities, including all six MicroDuck variants, spawn on Newton MJWarp.
- `test_microduck_velocity.py` — 4 passed:
  - deployed interface (61/76 inputs, policy term order, action joint order), per-reset BAM friction, 20 finite default-preset steps, and a NaN-injected environment that terminates alone with finite rewards and observations (flat);
  - foot height from ray hits, including misses, step undersides, and world elevation (synthetic);
  - rough terrain: contact parameters authored on the terrain mesh, finite foot rays at tile height, and foot heights;
  - `presets=backlash`: distinct play angles per joint and environment reach the policy and critic encoders and head rewards, play stops incur no limit penalty, 20 steps stay finite, and play joints stay undriven.
- `test_contrib_environments_kitless.py -k MicroDuck` — passed; it samples one task per family and steps `IsaacContrib-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck` with the default preset.
- `test_newton_manager_abstraction.py` — 114 passed (combined notifications, CUDA graph capture/recapture); `test_articulation.py -k hard_reset` — passed.
- `tools/update_environments_rst.py --check` — up to date; `tools/changelog/cli.py check` — passed; `make -C docs current-docs` with warnings treated as errors — passed; pre-commit hooks — passed.
- Before the rebase: flat and rough, with and without `presets=backlash`, 30 random-action steps stayed finite (14 or 28 joints; experiment names `microduck_velocity_{flat,rough}[_backlash]`; solver iterations 10/100), and regression tests (shared per-environment delay, torque feedback with sag, zero-Coulomb seeding, damping resync, configuration replacing existing USD values, play-angle read) failed without their fixes. Supplied `velocity_flat.onnx` (original Lab checkpoint, iteration 49,999) on the flat task, 32 envs × 1,000 control steps:

| Playback condition | Falls | Timeouts | Mean planar velocity error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed 0.15 m/s forward, play mode | 0 | 32 | 0.136 m/s |
| Training commands, corruption and disturbances | 0 | 32 | 0.185 m/s |

  This shows the existing policy runs stably, not exact parity with the old dynamics.

## Known limitations

- `DriveBam` registers the `NewtonBamDriveAPI` token when `isaaclab_newton` loads Newton articulations, so USD files with pre-authored BAM prims cannot be parsed on PhysX/OVPhysX.
- `applied_effort` reports motor torque; solver friction is read from `drive.friction_budget`.
- Groups and robots that Newton merges into one drive share its supply and delay per environment, and must agree on start-up ranges, `stiff_frictionloss`, and `backlash_joint_template`.

## Not in this PR

- MicroDuck fall-recovery task.
- Golden regeneration tooling; provenance (BAM commit, mjlab version, settings) is stored in the NPZ metadata.

## Follow-ups

- Add collision properties to `TerrainImporterCfg` and drop the task-local importer.
- Replace `delayed_observation` with core `ObservationTermCfg.delay_*`. Kept for parity: the IMU lag is redrawn on a fixed 64-step period with a per-environment phase, whereas core redraws with a per-sample hold probability.
- Find the source of the occasional non-finite MJWarp states and drop the observation guards; reset-time CoM randomization on Newton is a candidate.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guidelines and ran `uv run isaaclab -f`
- [x] Added tests that fail without the change
- [x] Updated docs (`concepts/actuators.rst` with a MicroDuck example, API reference, 3.0 migration guide)
- [x] Added changelog fragments (`isaaclab`, `isaaclab_newton`, `isaaclab_assets`, `isaaclab_tasks`; `.skip` for test-only `isaaclab_physx` / `isaaclab_ov`)

items.title: B72: opt-in producer-rate sampling for sensing.read_aligned
items.body:
## B72: opt-in producer-rate sampling for `sensing.read_aligned`

Closes the ROADMAP Perception gap left after B50: "producer-rate sampling (the pairing sees only captures that reads admitted)".

### Problem (premise test, passes on main)
B50's `read_aligned` pairs a fresh reference capture only among the captures that READS admitted to the hub. Its skew therefore depends on when the caller reads. The IMU can have produced a sample at the camera's capture instant that no read ever saw. The pairing then takes a farther capture, often stale.

### Mechanism (all opt-in; absent = byte-identical, pinned by golden tests)
- **Producers record at publication, bounded.**
  - `MobileBridgeController(state_history=N)` (bridge CLI `--state-history N`, 1..256) keeps its last N completed states exactly as `state` would serve them, each with its own publication time.
  - It advertises `state_history` in `hello` (capability + size) and serves the states to reader channels as `state_history(after_step)`. These are copies of history, never a refresh, and a new epoch empties them.
  - Without the option, `hello` is unchanged and the op is refused. The flag is absent from the recorded arguments unless given.
  - In process, `BufferedSensorProvider(descriptor, history=N)` records its last N publications.
- **Reader.** `BaseTruthReader.history(after_step)` checks:
  - the advertised bound
  - the reply epoch
  - every state's identity
  - that steps and physics times strictly advance past `after_step`

  One reply has one receipt time, and every age includes the round trip. `MobileStateSensorProvider.read_produced` and `EmbodimentBoundProvider.read_produced` (payload contract re-checked) build on it.
- **Hub.** `SensorHub.enable_produced(N)` (before seal), `read_produced` and `produced`:
  - Each fetch runs through the sensor's own bounded worker, deadline and quarantine.
  - Samples are admitted under the read rules: identity, one epoch per sensor (shared with reads), strictly increasing sequence, capture time and receipt.
  - A violating batch is refused whole and its watermark does not move.
  - A sample that is stale or over the packet bound is seen but never admitted, not even when presented again.
  - Each sensor's ring holds at most N samples and `max_history_bytes`, apart from the shared read history, so RGB-D cannot evict IMU samples.
- **Domain.** `alignment.producer_history: N` (1..256; bool, float and string are refused) makes `read_aligned` do the following:
  - It reads each paired sensor once, then fetches its producer history. A refusal is reported as `producer_error`.
  - It pairs among both sets (`merge_captures`: capture-time order, one copy per capture, the read copy kept).
  - B50's classification is unchanged: nothing interpolated, ties keep the earlier sample, stale and missing values withheld, another epoch or clock domain never aligned, saturation or rate × skew uncertain.
  - Each pairing reports `from_producer`, and the policy reports `producer_history`.
- `mobile_state_offload.READ_ONLY` now includes `state_history`. The guard test `test_mobile_state_server.py` pins that set and was updated.

### Measured (CPU, `tests/test_producer_rate_alignment.py`)
Setup:
- Real loopback mobile bridge, reached through MCP (`McpSkillServer` → RobotRuntime → `mobile_rgbd` + `mobile_state` providers).
- Two domains on the same bridge: `read_time` and `producer`.
- One camera capture every 6 physics steps (33.3 Hz at 5 ms), 24 captures.
- `read_aligned` polled 0–5 steps (0–25 ms) after each capture, each delay used 4×.
- `max_skew_s` 7.5 ms, `max_rotation_rad` 0.01; IMU yaw ≈3 rad/s, joints 0.5 rad/s.
- Deterministic stepping: explicit publishes, no free-running thread.

| IMU/joints rate | mode | IMU | joints | \|skew\| mean / median / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 Hz | read-time | 4 aligned / 4 uncertain / 16 stale | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 9.167 / 10 / 15 ms |
| 200 Hz | producer ring | 24 aligned | 24 aligned | 0 / 0 / 0 ms |
| 50 Hz | read-time | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 8 aligned / 16 stale | 8.333 / 10 / 20 ms |
| 50 Hz | producer ring | 12 aligned / 12 stale | 12 aligned / 12 stale | 5 / 5 / 10 ms |

- At 200 Hz, 40 of the 48 read-time pairings took a farther capture although a closer one had already been produced. 32 of those were stale and 4 uncertain (IMU, +5 ms at 3 rad/s). The ring never paired a farther capture (`ring_farther` = 0).
- At 50 Hz, 8 of the 48 read-time pairings took a farther capture than one already produced, and all 8 were stale; the ring aligned them. A capture that falls between two produced samples stays stale at −10 ms. The ring cannot invent the missing instants, and nothing is interpolated.
- The bridge runner (`scripts/isaac_microduck_bridge.py --state-history 8`, CPU software backend) records every completed step it publishes.

### Tests
- New file `tests/test_producer_rate_alignment.py`, 60 tests.
- **RED** on an export of origin/main 38f6d08: `55 failed, 5 passed in 1.43s`. The 5 that pass do so by design:
  - the premise test
  - 3 goldens: default `read_aligned` digest `641a62f2…2635`, B50's shipped-catalog digest, and default `hello`/no `state_history`
  - the default-off bridge runner
- **GREEN**: `60 passed`.
- With `test_proprio_time_alignment.py` + `test_mobile_state_server.py`: `132 passed`.
- **Related set** (63 files touching the changed modules): `1 failed, 1948 passed, 6 skipped`.
  - The 1 failure is `test_mobile_effects::test_pre_admission_travel_never_confirms_an_inert_command` (`reader_timeout`; the fixture's `read_timeout_s` is 0.04 and the box load was ~17).
  - That file passes alone: `329 passed`.
- **Mutation** on a scratch copy: 83 mutants across all 9 changed modules plus the CLI, **83/83 killed** (unmutated: `155 passed`).
  - The first run left 1 survivor: the reader's step-order check, because the reversed tamper also reversed times.
  - Fixed by adding the `step` tamper (steps 1,2,3,3 at increasing times).
- **Full suite** (rebased head 1388108 = origin/main 38f6d08 + 1): `3 failed, 10790 passed, 346 skipped, 4 deselected, 2 warnings in 1632.20s`, `EXIT=1`. The 3 failures are exactly the known MuJoCo placement ones; baseline 38f6d08 was `3 failed, 10730 passed`, and 10730 + 60 new = 10790.

### Not claimed
- The native skew distribution on Isaac, with or without the ring.
- A fusion estimator that consumes the pairings.
- Hardware clock synchronization.
- Producer history through the off-GIL `--state-reader process` reader. A handed-off reader channel refuses `state_history`, so the pairing reports `producer_error` and falls back to read-time sampling.
- `--state-history` on the H2 owner.
- Producer history for RGB/RGB-D providers (the reference is read fresh).

### Follow-ups
- Fusion estimator over the aligned pairings (ROADMAP Perception, still open). It is the natural next step and was not done here.
- `state_history` on the off-GIL state reader (`mobile_state_server` frame ops) and on the H2 owner.
- The live Isaac distribution (below).

### Live validation owed (parent, Isaac/Newton MicroDuck bridge, GPU 0)
1. Start an owned MicroDuck bridge with `--camera-rgbd --state-history 64`. Use the same recipe as the stream07 / B50 runs (docs/CUVSLAM_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md "Live native RGB-D stream", docs/OBSERVED_RGBD.md), a new output dir `<run>`, and the default in-process state reader (not `--state-reader process`). Check that `BRIDGE_LISTENING.json` → `hello.capabilities` lists `state_history` and that `hello.state_history == 64`.
2. Standing (zero policy commands). This is a passive reader that never steps or commands:
   ```
   env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONPATH=<merged-checkout>/src CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 <venv>/bin/python \
     /home/johnny/Projects/demo/cascade-lab/HERMES_BACKLOG_20261009/producer-rate-alignment/live/measure_producer_alignment.py \
     --run-dir <run> --producer-history 64 --samples 200 --period-s 0.05 --max-skew-s 0.0075 \
     --max-rotation-rad 0.02 --out <run>/b72-standing.json
   ```
   This script was smoke-tested on a CPU loopback bridge from the test fixtures: close ok, `ring_farther` 0, `producer_errors` 0.
3. Run the same command during a walk/turn episode commanded by the bridge owner, with `--out <run>/b72-walking.json`.
4. From each JSON, report:
   - `summary.sensors.{read_time,producer}/{imu,joints}`: statuses, `abs_skew_s` quantiles, reasons, `from_producer`, `producer_errors`
   - `summary.cases`: `ring_farther` must be 0
   - `reference_refusals` and both `close.ok`

### Proposed AGENTS.md line
> **Producer-rate sampling (B72):** a producer records the samples it publishes only behind an explicit bounded option (`state_history=N` / `--state-history N`, `BufferedSensorProvider(history=N)`). The hub admits them under the read rules into a per-sensor ring (`enable_produced`), and `read_aligned` pairs among read and produced captures only with `alignment.producer_history`. The classification stays B50's: never interpolate, and never let a produced sample bypass identity, epoch, ordering or age admission.

### Docs
- ROADMAP Perception row: producer-rate sampling struck, with a landed line, the measurement and what stays open.
- ARCHITECTURE: mechanism bullet, `sensing/` module map, Known limitations.
- ROBOT_MODULARITY: new section "Producer-rate sampling (B72, opt-in)"; B50's not-claimed item struck.
- OBSERVED_RGBD: pointer.
- `configs/robots/mixed_mock.yaml`: commented `producer_history` example. The sensors `alignment:` block lives in robot profiles, as with B50; `configs/demo.yaml` has no sensing block.

items.title: audit: MicroDuck Manager-Based API 能力对照 microduck_rl
items.body:
## 审计目标

对照 `/home/tatp/ws/simulator/microduck_rl`，确认运行模式并逐项审计 UniLab 的 Manager-Based API 能力，重点覆盖 observation/action/command/reward/termination/event(domain randomization)/curriculum/metrics/recorder 及任务注册覆盖。

审计基线：

- 参考实现：`microduck_rl` 当前工作树，`src/mjlab_microduck/tasks`
- UniLab：`dev/issue-1042-manager-based-api`
- UniLab manager 来源/适配：pinned mjlab manager API 的 NumPy/SimBackend 适配

## 运行模式结论

`microduck_rl` 明确是 Manager-Based：

- 任务配置文件均使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnvCfg`
- 导出和 testbench 使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnv`
- `scripts/testbench_sim2real.py` 手动复现 `ManagerBasedRlEnv.step()` 的 decimation 生命周期
- 在 `src/`、`scripts/`、`tests/` 未发现 `DirectRLEnv`、`DirectRlEnv` 或 direct-mode 入口

UniLab 也使用 `ManagerBasedRlEnvCfg` + `ManagerBasedRlEnv`，并接入唯一 `NpEnv` lifecycle；不是通过 direct mode 绕过 manager contract。

## 任务注册覆盖

参考实现 `src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/__init__.py`：

- 18 个基础任务：Velocity flat/rough、VelStand、StandUp、SitStand、GroundPick、BallKick、Rollers、Swizzle、RollerCrouch、RollerSlope、RollerStandUp、Spin、Roulade
- 15 个 backlash 变体
- 合计 33 个 task IDs

UniLab `src/unilab/tasks/locomotion/microduck/__init__.py` 当前只注册：

- `MicroduckVelocityFlat`
- backend：`mujoco`、`mjwarp`

因此按 task-ID 计，尚有 32 个参考任务未迁移；rough velocity 也不在当前 UniLab 注册范围内。

## 能力矩阵

| 能力面 | 参考实现证据 | UniLab 当前证据 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ManagerBased env/config/lifecycle | `ManagerBasedRlEnv(Cfg)`；manager 顺序由 env lifecycle 驱动 | `src/unilab/envs/manager_based_rl_env.py`：统一 `NpEnv`、reset/step、partial reset、auto-reset、final observation | **Implemented (adapted)** |
| Manager core | Action/Observation/Reward/Termination/Event/Command/Curriculum/Metrics/Recorder 全套 managers | `src/unilab/managers/` 具备 9 类 manager、term cfg、SceneEntityCfg、Null managers、shape/finite diagnostics | **Implemented (adapted)** |
| Observation groups | actor/critic、noise、history、delay、privileged foot observations | `microduck_velocity_flat/base.yaml` 声明 policy/critic；IMU 0–1 step delay、joint velocity 1 step delay、noise、critic privileged terms；ObservationManager 支持 history/delay | **Implemented for velocity flat; Partial for full task set** |
| Actions | 当前参考 MicroDuck 配方主要使用 JointPositionAction，但 manager catalog 还提供多种 action term | UniLab 当前 MicroDuck 仅接入 JointPositionAction；通用 manager 没有参考侧的全部 effort/velocity/relative/tendon/site/differential action catalog | **Partial** |
| Commands | 参考 `mdp.py` 含 UniformVelocity、VelocityCommandCommandOnly、RelativeHeadingVelocity、GroundPickPhase、UniformPose、SitStand 等 | UniLab MicroDuck 只有 `MicroduckVelocityCommand(Cfg)`、`UniformVectorCommand(Cfg)`；没有 GroundPick/SitStand/relative-heading 等专用 command | **Partial** |
| Rewards | `src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/mdp.py` 约 7.2k 行，含 walking/recovery/roller/spin/ground-pick/ball-kick/roulade 等大量 task terms | UniLab 有通用 velocity/gait/sensor rewards，MicroDuck 私有 terms 主要是 head/leg pose、biped air-time、flight phase；velocity flat YAML 的 18 项 reward 已有 focused contract | **Partial** |
| Event / domain randomization | 参考侧含 reset/startup/interval/step，BAM per-world model fields、mass/inertia、gains、damping/friction、COM、base orientation、ball/reset state 等 | UniLab 有 GeomFriction、JointArmature、PdGains、mass/COM、gravity、push、encoder bias 等 NumPy/SimBackend terms；对直接 model-field mutation 明确 construction-time fail-closed，未实现 BAM `requires_model_fields` | **Partial; BAM path Unsupported** |
| Curriculum | 参考侧含 terrain levels、velocity/heading/push/wheel curricula、reward weight、command range、event parameter 等 | UniLab CurriculumManager + staged reward/termination/command/event curriculum；velocity flat 已配置 action-rate、head bias、standing、head range、base/head COM 六条 ladder | **Partial** |
| Termination/reset | 参考侧除 timeout/fall 外还有 terrain bounds/edge、illegal contact、task-specific recovery/impact 条件及多种 reset state | UniLab 当前 MicroDuck flat 有 timeout/tilt/base-height/NaN 和默认 scene reset；缺少其他任务族的 task-specific reset/termination | **Partial** |
| Metrics/Recorder | 参考 velocity base config 有 `mean_action_acc` metric，任务还有专用统计/调试路径 | UniLab MetricsManager/RecorderManager 已实现并测试，但 MicroDuck owner 当前没有完整参考 metrics/debug GUI wiring | **Partial** |
| Viewer/debug API | 参考 manager 暴露 command/reward/event debug-vis、GUI hooks | UniLab NumPy runtime 有意不引入 viewer/Warp/model mutation；这些差异需在兼容矩阵中保持显式 Unsupported，不能宣称 parity | **Intentional difference / Unsupported** |
| Actuator/backend | 参考含 BAM XL330 friction/backlash actuator 与 15 个 backlash tasks | UniLab 当前 XML position-PD + MuJoCo/MJWarp owner；BAM/backlash 未接入，且 deploy notes 已记录该 gap | **Unsupported** |

## 已验证的正向结论

以下不是空壳能力，已有代码和测试证据：

- Manager core、Hydra/Registry materialization、NumPy term pipeline、partial reset、NaN/Inf diagnostics
- velocity flat 的 61D actor / 76D critic observation contract
- command range/resampling、IMU/joint-velocity delay、noise、foot privileged observations
- velocity flat 的 reward、termination、reset event、foot friction、armature、COM、push
- staged reward/command/event curriculum
- focused test result：

```text
uv run pytest -q tests/managers \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_velocity_contract.py \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_microduck_rewards.py \
  tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_mjwarp_dr_smoke.py

72 passed, 3 deselected
```

另外，MuJoCo 实际 reset/step slow test：

```text
uv run pytest -q tests/envs/locomotion/microduck/test_velocity_contract.py -m slow
1 passed, 2 deselected
```

MJWarp 完整 CUDA smoke 因当前环境没有 active CUDA Warp device 被 deselect，不能据此宣称 GPU runtime 已完整验证。

## 关键审计判断

1. “UniLab 已有 Manager-Based framework”成立。
2. “UniLab 已完成 microduck_rl 全部 Manager-Based API / task parity”不成立。
3. #1402 的 velocity recipe 验收只证明当前 velocity owner 的纵向配方；不能外推为 33 个参考 task、BAM/backlash、全部 task-specific command/reward/event/curriculum 均已迁移。
4. 对缺失的 model-field/BAM/viewer 能力，应保持显式 Unsupported/fail-closed；不能通过 warning、skip、zero fallback 或旧 direct env 掩盖。

## 建议后续切片

- 为 32 个未迁移 task ID 建立按 family 的 child issues（recovery、ground-pick/ball、rollers、spin/roulade、backlash），每个 child 同时包含 config、term、registry、测试和文档。
- 先建立 source-to-UniLab parity fixture：自动列出每个 owner 的 command/reward/event/curriculum/termination/observation keys，避免只测单个 velocity owner。
- 对 `GroundPickPhaseCommand`、`SitStandCommand`、`RelativeHeadingVelocityCommand`、roller/spin/roulade rewards 和 task reset states 明确迁移或 Unsupported 决策。
- 对 BAM `requires_model_fields`/recompute 能力单独开公共 backend contract issue；本审计不把它伪装成已支持。
- 在实现 PR 的最终 head 上执行 `make test-all`，并维护 Compatible / Adapted / Unsupported 矩阵。

相关 issue：#1042、#1401、#1402、#1425。

items.title: Roadmap: microduck 任务与上游 microduck_rl 训练配方逐步对齐
items.body:
## Owner summary

microduck 三个任务（velocity_flat / sitstand_flat / ground_pick_flat）已迁移到 UniLab，PPO 算法层与上游 microduck_rl 已基本一致（同为 rsl-rl-lib 5.0.1、超参逐项相同、obs 61D/76D 布局镜像），但物理层与 MDP 层存在实质差异，导致相同后端（MuJoCo Warp）下训练曲线不可比。本 roadmap 定义一个集成结果：**在 mjwarp 后端下，UniLab 的 microduck 训练与上游 microduck_rl 达到统计口径一致**（reward 曲线趋势、episode length 分布、收敛速度），逐轨迹 bit 级一致明确不做（两边随机源体系不同，接触动力学混沌，物理上不可能）。推荐按"物理层 → MDP 层 → 训练基建 → 受控对比验收"分 4–5 个 child issue 推进，每个都是可独立审查和回退的纵向切片。预计 5 个 PR、约 20–30 个 touched files、手写改动以 YAML/测试为主约 1.5k–3k LOC。永久维护责任：一份 microduck 对齐 contract 测试（防止配方漂移）、一套受控对比 benchmark 脚本、相应文档。**需要 maintainer 决定**：①执行器路线——是否复刻上游 BAM 电压伺服（最大差异源，工程量与长期责任显著，可作为独立 roadmap），还是本轮只对齐 PD 口径下的其余全部差异；②reward 栈对齐目标——上游当前 HEAD 还是现 base.yaml 所镜像的旧 velocity2 版本；③对比 benchmark 的训练预算（等效上游需 ≥1500 iter 的 GPU 资源）。

## 一句话问题

UniLab 的 microduck 配方按上游旧版 velocity2 镜像（`src/unilab/conf/ppo/task/microduck_velocity_flat/base.yaml:1-8`），且物理积分、执行器模型、reset/DR 分布与上游当前 HEAD 存在多处已核实差异，两边同走 MuJoCo Warp 也无法期望训练统计一致。

## 当前证据（两边仓库事实对照）

已核实的对齐项 ✓：rsl-rl-lib 同为 5.0.1；PPO 超参逐项相同（(512,256,128) elu、epochs 5、mini 4、lr 1e-3 adaptive desired_kl 0.01、γ 0.99、λ 0.95、clip 0.2、entropy 0.01、num_steps_per_env 24、obs normalization 双开、init_std 1.0 scalar）；obs 61D/76D 布局、noise/delay 结构、encoder bias、IMU misalignment 镜像上游；commands 与 5 条 curriculum stage step 一致；两边 reward 均 ×dt=0.02。

已核实的差异项 ✗（按对训练影响排序）：

1. **执行器**：上游 BAM 电压控制伺服（kt/R、m6 摩擦参数、电流限幅、电压 DR、15–30ms 命令延迟、每 substep 重算摩擦写 `dof_frictionloss`）；UniLab 为 XML `<position kp=50 kv=0.5>` PD（`src/unilab/assets/robots/microduck/microduck.xml:41-50`），`src/unilab/tasks/locomotion/microduck/sim2real_notes.py:9-12` 已自认此差距。
2. **物理积分**：上游 sim dt 0.005s × decimation 4（200Hz 物理）+ mjlab 注入 implicitfast / newton / iterations=10 / ls_iterations=20；UniLab `base.yaml:60` 为 `sim_dt: 0.01`（2 substep），且 XML 无 `<option>` → 全部 MuJoCo 默认（Euler、iterations=100）。
3. **Reward 栈漂移**：tracking_lin_vel 3.0 vs 2.0、head_pose_tracking 0.5 vs 2.0；UniLab 多 orientation(-3.0) / base_height(-50.0) / alive(+0.1) / flight_phase / lin_vel_z；上游有 upright(2.0) / variable_posture / self_collisions 等 UniLab 没有的项。termination 多处 `base_height<0.08`。
4. **初始分布与 DR**：上游 reset_base 有 xy±0.5 / z∈[0.12,0.13] / yaw±π 随机化 + startup mass/inertia DR（×[0.95,1.05]）；UniLab reset 严格回 keyframe 零速度、无 mass DR。push_robot 在 UniLab 为 `is_global_time=true`（全 env 同步），上游为 per-env。
5. **训练基建**：num_envs 2048 vs 4096、max_iterations 500 vs 50000（500 iter 仅 12000 env step，curriculum 只到第一档）、seed 1 vs 42、mujoco-warp 3.10.0.3 vs 3.8.1；UniLab env 级 RNG 不播种（`manager_based_rl_env.py:225-227` 用 `secrets.randbits`）；`init_at_random_ep_len=True` 在 rsl_rl 5.0.1 下实际无效（只写 wrapper 的 torch buffer，不影响 env timeout 计数）。

## 推荐方案

按依赖顺序分 5 个 child issue（粒度遵循"可独立交付、验证、回退"）：

1. **对齐基线与对比设施（research/benchmark）**：把上方差异清单落成机器可检查的对照 contract 测试（沿用 `scripts/audit_sim2sim_contracts.py` 的思路）+ 固定 seed 短程统计对比脚本；产出基线报告。这是后续所有 child 的验收标尺。
2. **物理层对齐**：sim_dt 0.005 / decimation 4；求解器参数显式声明（XML `<option>` 或 owner YAML 冷路径注入，遵守 hot-path 不碰 asset 的原则）；reset 分布、mass DR、push per-env 化、termination 对齐。
3. **MDP/reward 栈对齐**：按 maintainer 选定的上游目标版本重做 reward/termination 栈；更新 `base.yaml` 头注的对齐基线声明。
4. **训练基建对齐**：num_envs、seed、env RNG 播种、`init_at_random_ep_len` 修复（rsl_rl 5.0.1 适配层）、max_iterations 预算。
5. **受控对比验收 benchmark**：相同预算下多 seed 对比 run，产出统计一致性报告（reward 曲线、episode length、收敛速度），作为 roadmap 最终验收。

依赖：1 先行；2、3、4 在 1 之后可按序或有限并行推进；5 收尾。执行器 BAM 复刻不在默认范围，若 maintainer 批准则单独立项。

### 执行器路线的三个真实选项（决策项①）

- **A. 本轮不对齐执行器（推荐起步）**：只消除其余全部差异，对比报告会定量呈现 PD-vs-BAM 这一剩余差距；长期成本为零新增。
- **B. 双方退化到相同 PD 口径做受控对比**：请上游侧以 `--no-bam` 口径对齐（上游 runtime 支持该路径），UniLab 不改执行器；科学对比干净，但不消除 UniLab 与上游默认配置的差距。
- **C. 在 UniLab 复刻 BAM**：最彻底，涉及执行器模型、电压/摩擦 DR、stiff frictionloss 求解器参数（solref=(-5e4,-2e2) 等）与 mjwarp 后端每 substep 控制律执行路径，预估独立 roadmap 规模，新增长期 support 责任。

## 交付边界

- 做：microduck 三个任务在 mjwarp 后端的统计口径训练对齐 + 防漂移 contract 测试 + 对比设施。
- 不做：逐轨迹 bit 级一致（不可能且不必要）；BAM 复刻（决策项）；mujoco 后端同步对齐（本 roadmap 只覆盖 mjwarp，mujoco 后端作为 sim2sim 契约的既有覆盖范围不动）；上游仓库本身的任何修改。

## 长期维护责任（显式决策项）

- 新增：microduck 对齐 contract 测试（配置层，随上游版本更新需人工重锚定）、对比 benchmark 脚本与报告模板。
- 若选 C：执行器模型 + 后端每 substep 控制路径，属 `SimBackend` 能力面扩展，需先更新本 owner summary 再确认。
- 不新增：公共 env contract、runner/lifecycle、常规 CI、support 等级均不变。

## Declared base 与验收

- Declared base branch：`main`；授权后创建 `dev/issue-<number>-microduck-rl-alignment` 集成分支。
- 每个 child PR：base 为集成分支，最终 head 跑本地 `make test-all`。
- 最终验收：child 5 的统计对比报告 + 集成分支最新 head 的 `make test-all` + base 为 `main` 的最终 PR 走远程 CI。

## 范围复核点

- 对比实验显示剩余差距集中于某一未列入清单的参数（如 mujoco-warp 版本差）时，回来更新差异清单与方案。
- 任何触及 `SimBackend` 接口、runner contract 或新 support 等级的发现，先更新 owner summary 请 maintainer 确认。

items.title: test(drivers/microduck): grade the degraded surface, not just the happy path
items.body:
## The half that was ungraded

`tests/drivers/microduck/test_microduck_driver_over_socket.py` drives the driver
against a real robotd socket and grades the path where everything works.
`drivers/microduck.py` was at **83%**, and every one of the 60 uncovered
statements was on the other side - the paths where the driver refuses, degrades
or gives up.

For a native hardware driver that is the wrong half to leave unchecked: a driver
whose failure surface is ungraded is one that can report success about a robot
that did not move. What was uncovered:

| Surface | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| `start_task` / `run_policy` refusals | The module's entire answer to "why does `mode="real"` not run a policy". Both name `send_action` as the route instead; a refusal that stopped naming it leaves a caller told "no" with no route to yes. |
| The connect ladder below the version check | Nothing listening, a refused handshake, a hang-up mid-handshake, a declined `robot.subscribe`, a `robot.health` that is explicitly best-effort. An operator reading "could not connect" cannot tell a missing daemon from a declined subscribe, and the two have different remedies. |
| The reader thread's tolerance of a bad line | It is the only route by which joints, IMU and pose reach the mesh, so a blank keepalive or a truncated line has to cost one frame rather than every future frame. |
| The id-correlation timeout accounting | An unanswered request must not leave its slot in `_pending`. |
| `stop()`, the `-> None` shutdown hook | It has no envelope, so the only thing it can get wrong is claiming a halt robotd declined - and `motion_stopped` is what an operator reads to decide whether the robot is safe to approach. |

## What this adds

31 cells across 7 classes. Every socket cell drives a genuine `AF_UNIX` server:
`MockRobotd` for the faithful protocol, and a small `_scripted_robotd` helper for
the misbehaviours a faithful server by definition does not exhibit - a refused
handshake, a hang-up mid-handshake, a blank line, a line that is not JSON, and a
daemon that connects cleanly and then declines every intent.

Nothing is mocked at the driver's own seam, so the NDJSON framing and the id
correlation are exercised rather than asserted about.

`drivers/microduck.py`: **60 -> 13 missing, 83% -> 96%**. The statement count is
**unchanged at 354**, which is the check that the docstring correction below
added no production statements.

## The docstring correction

`map_hardware_joints` justifies its positional fallback as letting a robotd whose
vector "grew or shrank" degrade "to a partial read, not a crash". The two
directions are not symmetric, and the docstring described both as the first one:

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 15 wide (the contract) | index 9 (`mouth`) dropped, 14 joints named |
| 3 wide | a partial read: 3 joints named |
| 16 wide | a **full** 14-joint read, index 9 no longer dropped, so all five right-leg joints are named one position early |

The behaviour is deliberately left alone. Making the fallback drop index 9 too
would fix the grown case and change the 14-wide case, and which of those a
14-wide vector is - robotd having dropped the mouth itself, or having dropped
some other joint - is not knowable from the width. So this corrects the sentence
rather than guessing at the contract, and the tests pin the 15-wide contract and
the short-vector partial read while claiming nothing about the grown case.

## Detection

Because this is a test change, the equivalent of "fails pre-fix" is showing each
cell fires on a mutation of the behaviour it grades. 13 mutations of
`drivers/microduck.py`, run against the new file and against the four sibling
microduck suites:

| Mutation | new file | siblings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control (no change) | 0 | 0 |
| `start_task` returns success | 2 | 0 |
| `run_policy` refusal stops naming the sim route | 1 | 0 |
| Hello reason drops robotd's own error text | 1 | 0 |
| `stop()` sets `motion_stopped` before the call | 1 | 0 |
| reader re-raises on an unparseable line | 1 | 0 |
| timeout path stops popping the pending slot | 1 | 0 |
| a discrete refusal drops its own label | 3 | 0 |
| `read_state` returns an empty success | 1 | 0 |
| `send_action` drops the finite-number check | 2 | 0 |
| `map_hardware_joints` fallback drops the mouth too | **0** | 0 |
| the corrected docstring reverted | 1 | 0 |
| a `robot.health` failure aborts the connect | 1 | 0 |
| `connect_eagerly` loses its idempotence | 1 | 0 |

12 of 13 detected. The eleventh row is the behaviour change described above, and
it fires nothing - which is the evidence that these cells leave the grown-vector
case unpinned rather than enshrining today's answer. `collected` was stable at 31
on every row, no sibling suite was disturbed by any mutation, and the source was
restored byte-identically afterwards.

## Still uncovered, deliberately

13 statements: two wire-command builders for the pose and mouth intents, the
reader thread's own `OSError` path and its stop-flag break, `close`'s two
double-fault handlers, the constructor's extra-kwargs debug line, and the
`tool_type` / `tool_spec` / `stream`-status accessors. Those are narrow races and
plain accessors; adding cells for them would move a number without grading a
promise, so they are left.

## Gate

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean over `strands_robots tests tests_integ` (1717 files).
- `mypy strands_robots tests tests_integ`: 24 errors, **0 attributable** - the same set as the base.
- Paired 483-path selection (all of `tests/drivers/` plus every suite that walks
  the tree, parses source, or reads docstrings, `Args:`, `Raises:`, `__all__` or
  `changelog.d`), the new file withheld from both sides: identical `collected
  22261` and `20 failed, 22164 passed, 76 skipped, 1 xfailed` on each, 20 == 20
  failing ids, **both `comm` directions empty**. All 20 reproduce on the base
  alone: 17 need `awsiotsdk`/`awscrt` from the `mesh-iot` extra (absent locally,
  installed in CI) and 3 are the lerobot-from-source `encode()` drift.
- The new file: 31 passed in 2.3s. `tests/drivers/microduck/` plus the guard
  `main` added since the merge-base: 126 passed.

No visual artifact: this grades a transport's refusals and a docstring, which is
none of policy, simulation, rendering, recording or an asset.

items.title: Add the PoliteBow task: bow the head from the walking stance and return
items.body:
An episodic trick the runtime triggers from its ground-pick slot: from the walking default pose (HOME/STAND2) the robot bows its **head** forward to a deep, polite angle, holds briefly, and brings it back up. The head stays well clear of the ground and the feet stay planted.

`publish/cli.py` and `README.md` have both used `Mjlab-PoliteBow-Flat-MicroDuck` as their worked example since the publish flow landed — this fills it in.

## Result

Trained and verified. Final policy (wandb `j5y9ppq9`, iteration 1399):

| term | final | max | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bow_pose` | **5.84** | 6.00 | ~1.5° tracking error (do-nothing floor is 3.09) |
| `bow_sagittal` | 0.96 | 1.00 | bows straight, no list |
| `upright` | 1.93 | 2.00 | trunk vertical |
| `leg_stance` | 1.89 | 2.00 | legs hold stance |
| `feet_grounded` | 1.99 | 2.00 | feet planted |
| `mean_episode_length` | 993 | ~1000 | full 20 s episodes |
| `fell_over` | 0.04 | — | essentially never |

All three curricula completed (`action_rate −2.0`, `neck_action_rate −0.5`, `push_magnitude 0.25`), so this is hardened under full-strength pushes, not calm-conditions-only. Every penalty ≤ 0 throughout; `nan_state` 0. Two runs, ~$0.95 of HF Jobs L4 time at 2.4 s/iteration.

## Approach

Built on `make_microduck_velocity_env_cfg` rather than mjlab's base template, so the DR / obs-noise / sensor-delay / IMU-misalignment / encoder-bias / BAM / NaN-guard stack stays in sync with the walking policy for free. Only the objective changes:

- `twist` becomes a `GroundPickPhaseCommand` (period 4 s, profile `0.30 / 0.40 / 0.62`).
- The walking reward stack is dropped; `phase_pose_track` + its L1 bootstrap track `neck_pitch`/`head_pitch` against a target interpolated HOME ↔ `BOW_POSE` along the phase blend. The rise pays exactly like the descent, so arriving at the bottom early buys nothing.
- `bow_sagittal` holds `head_yaw`/`head_roll` at HOME; `leg_stance` keeps the legs near HOME at std 0.25, loose enough to counterbalance a 38%-of-body-mass head.
- `head_pose`/`body_pose` commands dropped, their obs slots zero-padded. Actor obs stays **61D**.

No new functions in `mdp.py` — this is the roller-crouch recipe pointed at a head keyframe.

## Two things measured, not guessed

**Keyframe depth.** Swept against the 71 mm fore/aft support polygon (head drop | beak angle | CoM front margin):

```
-0.70 / +0.40    67 mm |  63° | 20.8 mm   <- run 1, read as too shallow
-1.00 / +0.60    93 mm |  90° | 16.6 mm   <- shipped
-1.20 / +0.70   104 mm |  70° | 15.8 mm
```

Depth is nearly free in balance terms; the binding constraint is the **beak angle**, which peaks at vertical and then falls as the head rotates past it and points back under the robot. So `-1.00/+0.60` is the deepest *sensible* bow, not merely a deep one.

Run 1 also settled a diagnosis worth recording: it tracked its target to within 1.3° while still looking shallow. Depth is set by the keyframe and only by the keyframe — more training would have changed nothing. The module docstring says so, so the next person doesn't buy GPU time to fix a keyframe.

**Reward gradient.** `BOW_POSE` initially included `head_yaw`/`head_roll` pinned at HOME. Since `phase_pose_track` averages its Gaussian over the joints it is given, those two scored a perfect 1.0 every step regardless of behaviour — standing still earned 4.55 of 6.00 (76%). Restricting the target to the moving joints dropped the floor to 3.09 and doubled the signal. `test_doing_nothing_scores_well_below_a_real_bow` guards it.

`RISE_END = 0.62` is also deliberate: `infer_policy.py` hands the ground-pick slot back at φ ≥ 0.7, and `ground_pick` carries a ⚠️ for overrunning it.

## Tooling

```
just smoke-bow                    # 64 envs, 5 iters, CPU, free, ~15 s
just train-bow [iters] [timeout]  # 4096 envs on HF Jobs (l4x1)
just resume-bow <run_id> ...      # continue from a wandb checkpoint
just sim-bow <run_id> [ckpt]      # export + watch it locally (press G)
```

AGENTS.md gains a note that the smoke test runs on CPU via `--gpu-ids None` — the default `gpu_ids=[0]` dies in `select_gpus` with an `IndexError` that reads as "this machine cannot train" rather than "pass a flag".

## Tests

18 new, **217 passing** overall: phase window vs the runtime handback, bow direction against measured kinematics, reward signs, the 61D layout and slot order, curriculum ordering, inherited NaN/BAM wiring, a numeric trajectory check, and the do-nothing-gradient guard. All CPU.

The `-Backlash-` twin takes the walk backlash robot, mirroring the base task's collision model.

items.title: The brain runs on the robot: ogma_host, three commissioned senses, and the instruments that found their bugs
items.body:
25 commits over `master`, all of them about the robot rather than the simulator. **No deployed control law changes** — there is no gait work here, no lever, and no A/B. The one piece of shared code that moves is `DiagPublisher`, which gains a bind address defaulting to loopback, so the Godot host is byte-identical.

## The brain runs on the robot

`ogma_host` is the third program SPEC 1 asked for. It links `ogma_core`, builds one `OgmaInstance` from a `GraphConfig`, bridges physical sensors onto `reality.*`, ticks at 50 Hz on an absolute-deadline loop, and serves the **existing** inspector protocol — the same `ControlServer` on `OGMA_INSPECTOR_PORT`, `DiagPublisher` on `port+1` — so `xaq_inspector` and `xaq_voice` needed no new interface. Idle cost is 0.068 % of the 20 ms budget at 0 overruns.

It has no servo path and no way to acquire one (SPEC 1.1), which is what makes it safe to leave running unattended.

`picrawler_senses.json` is authored *for* hardware rather than ported to it: three Level-0 EPMs over the inputs the robot physically has — mic → STFT, camera → JL at the retinal encoder's 32×32×1, ultrasonic → RBF — fused by a `LateralVoter`. The gait configs could not run here anyway; five of their twelve topics are oracle-fed by the sim. Every input in this one is egocentric by construction.

Both daemons now have systemd units. `ogma-host.service` asks for `SCHED_FIFO` and is granted `CAP_SYS_NICE`, verified in the log rather than assumed.

## The three senses, commissioned

Each of these was a wrong answer that looked like a working one, and in every case the instrument came before the diagnosis.

- **The ultrasonic is on D2/D3, not D0/D1.** The BOM had it wrong in two places. Established without driving anything: hold every D pin as an input and read it under an internal pull-up, then a pull-down — a pin a device drives ignores the pull, a floating pin follows it. Echo width now comes from libgpiod v2 kernel edge timestamps rather than a poll loop: spread 866 µs ± 3 µs, about ±0.5 mm.
- **The camera was reading across frame boundaries.** rpicam-vid's YUV420 Y plane has a row pitch that is not the width — on this ISP, the width rounded up to a multiple of 128. The operator saw it first, as "a repeating pattern whose TLE pulses and does not change when I move".
- **The range channel was encoding noise.** The report was "the encoder only outputs on change". `range_tool` cleared the sensor in ten seconds — 92.4 cm held to ±0.4 cm, 89 of 89 pings valid — which located the fault in the conditioning rather than the rangefinder. The rate dimension is gone and the distance is commissioned.
- **A no-echo ping reported 0 cm** — the nearest possible reading for the farthest possible condition. Out-of-range is now its own channel, not a silent substitution.
- **The GNGs stalled, and it was conditioning** (`CLAUDE.md` §0 rule 4). The audio EPM sat at 2 nodes because the mic's capture gain was at 0 of 0–16, putting room tone at −74 dBFS — the STFT features never reached the insertion gate. `insertion_autotune` is not the fix; it takes the configured value as a floor. +23.8 dB of hardware gain took that GNG 2 → 29 nodes with TLE tracking the input and `is_novel` firing. Vision reached 7 on a static scene, range stayed at 2 — the honest answer for a wall at a fixed distance. Node count alone would have read as a broken EPM; it was a quiet room.
- The range EPM's input ranges are now **calibrated and stored** — derived by `dim_autocal_ticks` over a 400-frame sweep, written into the config, autocal removed.

## Instruments

- **A tick-budget and memory meter** (`ResourceMonitor`), reported as per cent of the *budget* rather than of a wall-clock second, because that is the quantity a control loop has. It reports p50/p95/max, because a mean is a blind metric — a loop averaging 15 % while spiking to 110 % every fortieth tick reads healthy and still misses its deadline. Wall and CPU time are kept separate: `wall ≫ cpu` means blocked and more compute is nearly free, `wall ≈ cpu` means compute-bound and every new module costs budget. Calibrated against synthetic load, not argued: 5.01 / 20.01 / 50.01 / 90.01 / 125.01 % for 1 / 4 / 10 / 18 / 25 ms. The 18 ms row is the argument for the whole thing — p50 90 %, max 104 %.
- **`picrawler-dash`** — the bench dashboard's numbers on a terminal, over ssh or a screen plugged into the robot, plus the thing Godot does not show: every EPM's nodes / baked / baked-fraction / ema_tle. It uses only stateless reads, so it cannot collide with the inspector.
- **The camera, in Godot** — `ogma_host` gains a PUB socket behind `--video` and a `VideoClient` GDExtension feeds the bench dashboard. Two planes per frame, and the pair is the point: what the camera sees (128×96, native aspect) beside what the brain is handed (the 32×32 centre crop). Colour was already arriving in the YUV420 frame and being discarded; **the brain's plane is still 32×32×1 by spec.** ~200 kB/s on the wire.
- **The inspector connects from its UI** — host fields under the module list, remembered across runs, so switching between a local Godot brain and the one on the robot no longer means relaunching with flags.
- **An INA219 driver** for the shared-rail brownout, at 532 µs resolution. The part is not fitted yet. Current is derived on the host from raw shunt counts and `r_shunt` is stored as calibration metadata rather than baked in, so a later re-fit re-derives old samples instead of stranding them. PGA defaults to /8 because the shunt LSB is 10 µV on every range — the widest costs no resolution and buys ±32 A at 1 mA. `pga_clipped` is surfaced loudly, since silently under-measuring inrush is the one failure this sensor exists to prevent.

## Fixes on the bench

- **Twelve servos starting at once brown the Pi out.** Reproduced: `pose.set(rescue)` from the X pose drove eight servos toward their 500 µs extremes at 2000 µs/s on the HAT's shared 5 V/3 A DC-DC; telemetry stopped 0.5 s later. The A4 battery reading never saw it — the sag is on the 5 V rail. Pose and rescue moves are now queued and started 100 ms apart at 600 µs/s, shortest travel first, with the driver watchdog fed for the whole move.
- **14 % of audio windows were being dropped.** Shortening the FFT window to fit inside the tick makes it worse; a continuous ring fixes it. Measured over 30 s afterwards: mic 0 drops, 0 ALSA xruns, camera 0, range 0.
- **The diag stream was loopback-only**, so no inspector on another machine could see it. The bind address is a constructor parameter defaulting to `127.0.0.1`; `ogma_host` opens it behind its own `--listen` flag. A diag stream is unauthenticated, so exposing it stays a deliberate act.
- **The robot is addressed as `picrawler.local`.** Onboard wifi had never worked — it was rfkill soft-blocked, which is why every configuration attempt failed with nothing useful to report. That exposed the real problem: `wlan0` gets a different DHCP address than `eth0`, so every hardcoded IP breaks the moment the cable comes out.
- Dashboard counters are **uptime and rates**, not running totals — "104569 frames" only restates how long the process has been up.

## Docs

BOM corrections (the D2/D3 pinout, the IMU's SPI, how to break the battery line), the day-2 bring-up log, the ledger, and the §7.5 band decision: **2.4 GHz, locked by BSSID.** The Pi had roamed onto the 5 GHz radio of the same SSID — −67 dBm, 20 % packet loss, 889 ms mean RTT against a 500 ms `BenchClient` timeout — while the 2.4 GHz radio sat 18 dB stronger with 0 % loss and 7 ms RTT. `802-11-wireless.band bg` is advisory and did not hold; a BSSID lock does. The warning travels with it: a BSSID lock does not roam.

## What was run

On this x86 laptop, on the branch head:

- `cpp_core` builds clean; **62 of 62 project test binaries pass**.
- `godot_host` builds `ami_ogma_host`.
- `pi_host` builds and `test_hw` is **25 of 25** — the degraded set, which is correct here: `ogma_sensors` and `ogma_host` are disabled without ALSA and libgpiod, exactly as intended.

Everything involving an actual sensor was measured on the Pi during bring-up and is reported in the commit messages; none of it was re-verified on this machine, and the 30-test set needs the Pi. This repository has no CI, so nothing gates the merge automatically.

## Not in scope

No gait work, no lever, no A/B — the simulated body is untouched. The INA219 is a driver for a part that is not installed. Four hardware installs remain parked on physical blockers (INA219, ICM-20948, VL53L0X, FSRs).

## Merge notes

Fast-forward onto `master`: 25 ahead, 0 behind. Zero file overlap with `microduck` or `microduck-lean-prior`, and a trial merge of either against this branch is conflict-free, so the two PRs can land in either order.

**This branch was force-pushed.** Its history was rewritten to replace a home SSID and an access point's BSSID in `§7.5` with placeholders — a BSSID is enough to place a house through the public wifi-positioning databases, and this repository is public. Only that one file and one commit message differ from the pre-rewrite branch. Anyone holding an older checkout should reset to the remote rather than merge.

items.title: Slice 1: robotd holds a pose, and health means something
items.body:
First of two slices toward M3. Design lives in `docs/robotd-design.md`, added here.

## Why this and not walking

The update engine is finished and has never run on hardware. Its auto-rollback is only meaningful if `robot.health` is a real measurement — and until now it meant *"the control loop ticked once"*. Every rollback tested so far was tested against a placeholder.

So slice 1 makes health honest rather than making the robot walk. `robotd` holds the pose it starts in, which puts the real load on the bus at the real rate — so timing and health are representative — while nothing falls over when a deliberately broken release lands. Install / rollback / power-cut cycles can be hammered at a bench all day. Walking is slice 2.

## What health means now

Three thresholds, all in `/etc/robot/robotd.toml`:

| check | catches |
|---|---|
| achieved rate below a floor | a loop at 60% of target — alive, answering, badly broken |
| no tick for N periods | a wedged control thread |
| consecutive bus read failures | a bus that has gone away |

Computed by the IPC side from atomics the loop publishes, never by calling into the loop — so a wedged loop reports itself unhealthy instead of hanging the caller.

## New crate: `duck-control`

Everything between reading the bus and writing it — robot model, Dynamixel bus, IMU, the `RobotIo` seam. No tokio, no sockets, no systemd, so the boundary against daemon concerns is enforced by the compiler rather than by discipline.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **`robotd` never moves the robot on its own.** It adopts the pose it finds and does not touch torque, so an update restart leaves a standing robot standing — the servos hold their goal while the process is dead, so there is no gap. Going to the home pose is an explicit `robotd init`. This is the decision that makes update testing safe on a robot that is standing up.
- **New bus code, borrowed numbers.** Conversion factors and the EEPROM registers asserted at startup come from `microduck_runtime`, where they were arrived at against hardware — each with a comment saying so. `return_delay_time = 0` is load-bearing: the XL330 ships at 250, which is ~8 ms of pure turnaround per tick across 16 devices, 40% of the budget.
- **The loop gets its own thread and its own current-thread runtime.** The bus read is blocking serial I/O; on a shared runtime it would occupy a worker for every transaction. Not an RT project — no `SCHED_FIFO`, no pinning. The acceptance criterion is *do not regress* against today's `bench_dynamixel_bus` numbers.
- **`DynamixelIo` is not `cfg`-gated off macOS.** The design originally said gate it; `rustypot` and `serialport` both build there, so the gate bought nothing and cost type-checking the bus layer on a laptop. Only the entry points that open a real port are gated — `--fake` must be asked for, never fallen back to.
- **Params are a file, not more flags.** Read once at startup, not watched. Outside the release dir so it survives update *and* rollback.

## Two things flagged rather than fixed

- Component-wise median over three unit gravity vectors is not itself unit-norm during a transient. Kept parity with the runtime (normalise, then median) rather than silently changing a path that currently walks. Commented, pinned by two tests, and flagged for slice 2 — if training expects strict unit norm, normalising *after* the median is the fix.
- The XL330 has a `bus_watchdog` register (addr 98). I had earlier claimed there was no bus-timeout failsafe; that was wrong. Whether it helps is still open — on X-series it zeroes goal velocity rather than cutting torque, so a position-held biped may just freeze.

## Testing

**272 passing** (up from 246), no hardware, no network, no Docker. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` both clean.

The existing gate test now drives a real control loop via `FakeIo` instead of a heartbeat — same assertions, real loop underneath. Smoke-tested the binary over its socket: `{"healthy":true}`, `{"safe":true}`.

Untouched deliberately: the two unresolved 61D command-encoding questions in `docs/robotd-design.md` §11.2 — slice 1 has no observations, so they do not bite yet.

items.title: strands-labs/robots roadmap | v0.3.9 → v0.4.0 → v0.5.0
items.body:
> **Pinned roadmap** -- releases, merged PRs, active work, what's next. > > **Current tag**: [`v0.5.1`](https://github.com/strands-labs/robots/releases/tag/v0.5.1) (shipped 2026-08-06) -- the latest published tag. Previous: [`v0.5.0`](https://github.com/strands-labs/robots/releases/tag/v0.5.0) (2026-08-04), [`v0.4.1`](https://github.com/strands-labs/robots/releases/tag/v0.4.1) (2026-07-01). > **State**: **`v0.5.0` (2026-08-04) and `v0.5.1` (2026-08-06) are both out**; the planned v0.4.2 patch was never cut, so the post-v0.4.1 wave shipped as a minor tag. `v0.5.0` published the Isaac Sim backend absorption (#1156, closing epic #1144), the remote policy inference client/server split (#1142), the floating-base state lane, the locomotion reward-term DSL composed into runnable go2/g1/t1 benchmarks, the terrain curriculum, the `describe()` discovery surface and the `lerobot>=0.6.0` floor (#1114). `v0.5.1` is a correctness-only patch over three days, headlined by the `lerobot>=0.6.1` floor that makes `stream_dataset(repo_type="bucket")` resolver-guaranteed rather than lucky (#1930). Since the **`v0.5.1`** tag a further **1,451 PRs** (#1987 -> #3750) have accrued on a fresh `[Unreleased]` wave -- **981 fixes + 158 test pins against 151 features**, 78.5% correctness. Its capability surfaces are the **native hardware-driver programme** (twelve buses across 25 registry robots, #2734 seam onward), the **agent-facing Unitree G1 verb surface** ported from `neon-the-g1` and then consolidated 79 modules -> 22 (#3037/#3070), two **humanoid policy providers** (`KimodoPolicy` #2270, `ProtoMotionsPolicy` #2287), **Isaac backend parity**, **photoreal 3DGS + GS-derived lighting**, the **VLM-judge** batch, **one drive contract for every mobile base** (#2689/#2696), the **dashboard** -- which in the newest band finally got a **server** (#3695), taking that package to fifteen modules plus a served `static/` bundle -- **FastTD3** (#3206), the **rollout observer lane** (#3351) and a **deployable RL checkpoint** through the policy factory (#3414). Roughly **116,000 lines** have come out across thirteen net-negative refactors, and **the newest band ends the featureless run at nine bands**: 73 PRs, **277 files, +18,945 / -682 -- net +18,263 lines**, the largest net-positive band this page has recorded, carrying **seven `feat`** commits after nine bands with none. The removals ledger is nonetheless unchanged for a fifth band (`vera`, `lerobot_calibrate`, `motionbricks`, `strands_robots.transforms`, the MolmoAct2 normalization port), the net-negative refactor table holds at thirteen, and for a fifth band the absence of a `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE` trailer is correct rather than a gap -- nothing public left `main`. **It also closed the oldest small item on this page: the `0000-` fragment placeholder defect is fixed** (#3715/#3721/#3722), so `changelog.d/` holds none for the first time since they appeared and sequencing item 6 is retired. Its recurring fix idioms each have a section below: a stop reports its outcome rather than asserting one; a published budget is measured on a clock that cannot step; a shared value domain replaces a hand-rolled bound; a posture flag is read as a value, not by truthiness; a refusal names a remedy that works; the whole-tree graders grade the whole tree; a span that resolves to no work is refused; a cache is served only while its key still names what the entry is about; a run that stopped early states how much never ran; one owner answers one question; a verdict names the thing it was written for; a store is written whole, or the previous one is still there; a telemetry field the frame does not carry is not a reading; an operator is asked before a command reaches a real actuator (#3418/#3420/#3430/#3431, widened to every unknown verb by #3508); a docs page states each contract once; a value that can never be honored is refused at the entry point (thirteen fixes, #3502 the sharpest); a resource a failed bring-up adopted is released (#3519/#3522/#3526/#3530/#3532); an action naming a key the surface cannot carry is refused (#3534/#3537/#3539); a name is held to the alphabet its consumers can carry (#3557/#3558/#3559/#3565/#3570); a run that commanded nothing is refused rather than scored (#3584/#3608/#3612/#3613/#3620, and now at the rollout entry point itself by #3680); a shutdown that cannot complete does not keep the resource (#3590/#3596/#3602/#3603); an offline snapshot names what the live registry registers (#3614/#3616/#3618/#3623); a criterion already satisfied at reset is reported, not read as a result (#3629/#3633/#3637/#3639/#3642); a plan that commands nothing is a failure, not a plan (#3643/#3652/#3655/#3657); a ROS 2 name must be able to name a topic (#3628/#3635/#3636/#3638/#3648/#3651); a reader grades the size its own payload declares (#3627/#3650/#3658); a refusal applies nothing from its own call (#3622/#3625/#3645); and now the band's own four: **an unreadable reply names the peer, not the codec** (#3670/#3672/#3676/#3677), **a configuration entry that is not a string is refused** (#3666/#3667/#3674/#3679), **a motion that did not reach names what stopped it** (#3703/#3705/#3727/#3733) and **a camera name answers for the camera it names** (#3683/#3691/#3693/#3730). **The tracker moved again after a band in which nothing moved at all**: two issues were filed and closed inside the band against merged code (#3664 via #3666, #3684 via #3686) and two more were filed and are still open (#3734, #3744), so open issues went 3 -> 5. The review queue went **11 -> 21**, the largest this page has recorded, and the extra-approval remedy is now the board's normal path rather than a novelty: **seven heads read `APPROVED`** (#3729, #3743, #3746, #3749, #3751, #3752, #3753). What still waits on a second account is #3205, #3343, #3427, #3496, #3515, #3577, #3615, #3714, #3726 and #3737 -- each green, armed, every thread resolved, and therefore still `REVIEW_REQUIRED` under `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes`. > **Status**: **CLOSED as completed 2026-08-14** -- this roadmap is retired. It stays pinned as the historical record of the v0.3.9 -> v0.4.0 -> v0.4.1 -> v0.5.0 -> v0.5.1 arc; live tracking is the `0.5.0` milestone and the open issues, not this document. Reconciled once more below so a pinned page does not read as current plan. > **Last synced**: 2026-09-16 against `main` @ #3750 -- **73 PRs** have merged since the previous marker, taking the wave to **1,451 PRs** (#1987 -> #3750) since the `v0.5.1` tag: 1,378 + 73 = 1,451. The band spans **#3661 -> #3750** with **two out-of-order merges** (#3661 and #3662, both rows on the previous Open-PRs table). Caveats for anyone recounting. **The counting streak broke again, and in the direction that under-reports**: the tip commit is **#3740** while **#3750** is the highest merged number, so a marker read off `git log`'s newest subject is ten short. Last sync's marker was also its tip, so a range taken from the #3660 commit yields exactly **73** commits for 73 new pull requests -- no trap this time. **The clean sweep broke after two bands, and it broke on the shape #3169 measured**: seventeen numbers inside #3661 -> #3750 are absent from `main` -- nine open pull requests (#3673, #3714, #3726, #3729, #3737, #3739, #3743, #3746, #3749), two open issues (#3734, #3744), two issues closed in band against merged code (#3664, #3684), and **four pull requests closed unmerged, every one a second implementation** (#3665 against merged #3666, #3671 against merged #3672, #3736 against merged #3731, and #3732 descoped into the fix #3733 plus the tracker item #3734) -- instances **sixteen to nineteen** of that shape, after two bands at zero. **The `0000-` placeholder defect is closed**: `changelog.d/` holds **none**, where it held four for three syncs, and the guard now refuses the number at every surface (#3715/#3721). One bookkeeping stray remains: #3702's body carries `Closes #767`, which names a pull request merged in the v0.4.1 wave rather than an issue, so it closed nothing. The two older caveats still stand: one wave commit carries no PR reference at all (`cff130dc`, a direct `test(isaac)` push), so `git log` shows **1,452** commits for 1,451 PRs -- measured exactly at this marker -- and #2801's squash title carries a shell-quoting artifact (`(#'2801')`), so a naive `(#NNNN)` grep returns 1,450. ## Where we are (2026-09-16 reconciliation) **No new tag since `v0.5.1` (2026-08-06)** -- it is 41 days old and still the latest published release, with **1,451 PRs** (#1987 -> #3750) accrued behind it. The day since the last sync added **73 PRs**, the largest band since 2026-09-11. Milestone `0.5.0` held at **11 closed / 0 open (100%)** for a nineteenth sync. **Open issues 3 -> 5.** **Open PRs 11 -> 21**, the largest review queue this page has recorded. **The featureless run is over at nine bands, and it ended on volume rather than on one feature.** 73 PRs: **58 `fix` + 7 `feat` + 4 `test` + 3 `docs` + 1 `refactor`**, **277 files, +18,945 / -682 -- net +18,263 lines**, the largest net-positive band here by a factor of nearly two. `feat` moves **144 -> 151**, `fix` **923 -> 981**, `test` **154 -> 158**, `docs` **109 -> 112**, `refactor` **24 -> 25**, and correctness still climbs, 78.2% -> **78.5%**, for a fourteenth consecutive sync -- because the fix count grew faster than the feature count even in the band that broke the streak. The one `refactor` is `examples`-scoped (#3709), so the net-negative refactor table holds at thirteen and **the removals ledger is untouched for a fifth band**: `vera`, `lerobot_calibrate`, `motionbricks`, `strands_robots.transforms` and the MolmoAct2 normalization port are still gone from `main` and still present in the last published tag. No commit carries a `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE` trailer, which is again correct rather than a gap. `_SHIPPED_DRIVERS` holds at twelve buses across 25 registry robot names and `strands_robots/tools/g1` at 22 modules; **`strands_robots/dashboard/` moves eleven -> fifteen** and gains a served `static/` bundle. **The seven features are the news, and six of the seven are one theme: the library says more about the thing it just handed you.** **#3695** is the largest -- **the dashboard finally has a server** (19 files, +1,609 / -74), the core wired to the rails the previous nine bands landed (`auth`, `access`, `consent`, `safety_state`, `settings`, `log_redaction`, `validate_scope`, `agent_hitl`) and **failing closed**, which is what the #2848 decomposition argument was for. Beside it **#3728** (`tool_frame` declares the tool point a site-less model lacks), **#3727** (`get_robot_state` says which way the arm extends from its base), **#3694** (SO-arm joints can be addressed by label rather than by index), **#3724** (`step` feeds an open dataset recording, so a hand-stepped scene records like a rollout), **#3731** (`Robot(tool_name=)` names the tool, so two robots of one type can share one Agent) and **#3697** (`render_dir` on the constructor moves the render sandbox per `Simulation`). **Its dominant fix shape is a refusal telling the truth about which side failed: an unreadable reply names the peer, not the codec.** Four clients decoded a peer's response inside a `try` that reported a codec error, so an inference server, a Cosmos3 world model, a MoveIt2 planner and a GR00T service each answered a malformed or truncated reply by blaming the local decoder -- which sends the caller to the wrong side of the wire. #3670, #3672, #3676 and #3677 each name the peer and what it sent. **Second, a configuration entry that is not a string is refused.** The mirror of the posture-flag lane, on the value side rather than the boolean side: a credential, a name-list entry or a body arrives as `None`, a number or a nested object, is stored, and is then dropped by whatever consumes it. **#3666** is the one with a tracker item behind it -- a DDS Security credential that is not a string was accepted and the participant QoS then dropped it, so a run believed it was authenticated (closes **#3664**) -- with #3667 (a dashboard settings list entry), #3674 (a mesh ACL `cert_common_names` entry) and #3679 (a Reachy daemon body that is not an object). **Third, a motion that did not reach names what stopped it.** The verified-halt lane asked whether a stop had stopped; this asks the same question of a *move*. **#3733** makes a `move_to` that fell short name the contact or the joint limit that stopped the servo, rather than reporting the pose it was asked for; **#3705** makes `set_gripper` say what the fingers closed on; **#3703** makes `attach_bodies` report whether the bodies actually touch; and the feature **#3727** answers the question underneath all three, which is which way the arm is pointing. **#3732 is the instructive part of this lane**: it was the `feat` version of the same idea, and it was closed unmerged in favour of the narrower fix #3733 plus a tracker item, **#3734**, for the `rotate_wrist` half -- a descope recorded rather than dropped. **Fourth, a camera name answers for the camera it names.** Four fixes on the surface that has produced more naming defects than any other: **#3683** (every camera name the sim lists can be rendered through it), **#3693** (a camera enumeration offers each camera once, not once per name), **#3691** (`add_camera`/`remove_camera` accept `camera_name` where every sibling does) and **#3730** (`start_recording` names the cameras by a name that answers for them). - **The featureless run ends at nine bands**: 73 PRs, 58 `fix` + 7 `feat` + 4 `test` + 3 `docs` + 1 `refactor`, **+18,945 / -682, net +18,263**; `feat` 144 -> **151**, correctness 78.2% -> **78.5%**. - **An unreadable reply names the peer, not the codec (4 fixes, new lane)**: #3670, #3672, #3676, #3677. - **A configuration entry that is not a string is refused (4 fixes, new lane)**: #3666 (closes #3664), #3667, #3674, #3679. - **A motion that did not reach names what stopped it (4, new lane)**: #3703, #3705, #3727, #3733. - **A camera name answers for the camera it names (4)**: #3683, #3691, #3693, #3730. - **Seven features, the dashboard server among them**: #3694, #3695, #3697, #3724, #3727, #3728, #3731. - **The `0000-` fragment defect is closed, and sequencing item 6 with it**: #3715 refuses the placeholder number, #3721 gives that rule one owner so every surface refuses it, #3722 renames the one fragment that named no PR. `changelog.d/` holds **zero** placeholders for the first time since they appeared. - **A rollout is exclusive, and one that commanded nothing is an error**: #3741 refuses `run_policy`/`eval_policy` while another rollout drives the robot; **#3680** carries the #3584 -> #3620 lane to the rollout entry point itself. - **A surface offers a next step the thing it just made can take**: #3686 (closes **#3684** -- `add_robot` had advertised `run_policy` for a model with zero actuators), #3687 (the sim tool description describes the world the agent is joining), #3719 (a paused real-robot call tells the script how to resume it), #3742 (an unreachable GR00T server fails fast and names the remedy). - **The dashboard's own correctness pass, same band as its server**: #3710 (a caller-supplied value cannot forge a log entry), #3738 (a credential store that parses but cannot serve as one is recovered, not answered with a 500). - **Four test pins**: #3662, #3669, #3675, #3745. - **The rest**: #3663, #3681, #3682, #3685, #3688, #3689, #3690, #3692, #3696, #3698, #3699, #3700, #3701, #3702, #3704, #3706, #3707, #3708, #3711, #3712, #3713, #3716, #3717, #3718, #3720, #3723, #3725, #3735, #3740, #3747, #3748, #3750. - **The earlier bands are unchanged and still the bulk of the wave**: the 81-PR g1 verb port (consolidated to 22 modules), the twelve-bus native-driver programme, the Isaac asset-reader run, the shared-value-domain sweep, Microduck hardening, the `doctor` lane, the whole-tree grader audit, the cache-validity lane, the mobile-base drive contract, FastTD3, the observer lane, the operator-consent lane, the docs diet, and the refuse-what-cannot-be-honored, release-what-a-failed-bring-up-adopted, checked-posture-flag, refused-payload-key, name-alphabet, commanded-nothing, failed-shutdown, offline-snapshot, criterion-already-satisfied, plan-that-commands-nothing, ROS-2-name, declared-size and refusal-applies-nothing lanes. Their sections below are unedited. **Release hygiene is still the only standing gap, and it is now 1,451 pull requests wide.** There is no `## [0.5.0]` or `## [0.5.1]` heading -- `CHANGELOG.md` has not been edited since #1690 (2026-07-28) -- `[Unreleased]` is still frozen at 168 entries, and the real accrual is still not in it: `changelog.d/` now holds **1,601** `.md` files, of which **1,600** are fragments (`README.md` is not one). The band added **70** and deleted none: 1,530 + 70 = 1,600 reconciles exactly, and `scripts/assemble_changelog.py --check` reports `OK (1600 pending)` -- collapsing both shipped tags remains a release action rather than a repair. **73 PRs produced 70 fragments**, the four `test` commits owing none and one PR carrying two, which is the convention working as intended. **What did change is the naming**: the four `0000-` placeholders are gone and the guard now rejects the number at every surface, so sequencing item 6 -- unactioned for three syncs -- is **closed**. **The gap between the fragments and the tag remains the page's oldest unaddressed item** -- 50 days since the last CHANGELOG edit, and every one of those 1,600 fragments is a release note nobody has read. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["v0.3.8
